**James William Buffett** (December 25, 1946 – September 1, 2023) was an American singer-songwriter, author, and businessman.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-NYT-20230909-11) He was known for his tropical music sound blending country, rock, folk, [calypso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calypso_music "Calypso music"), and his persona,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-insideme-3) which often portrayed a lifestyle described as "island [escapism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escapism "Escapism")."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-NYTObit-12) It promoted enjoying life and following passions.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-13) Buffett recorded many hit songs, including those known as "The Big 8":[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-14) "[Margaritaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaritaville "Margaritaville")" (1977), which is ranked 234th on the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America")'s list of "[Songs of the Century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songs_of_the_Century "Songs of the Century")"; "[Come Monday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Monday "Come Monday")" (1974); "[Fins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fins_(song) "Fins (song)")" (1979); "[Volcano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcano_(Jimmy_Buffett_song) "Volcano (Jimmy Buffett song)")" (1979); "[A Pirate Looks at Forty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Pirate_Looks_at_Forty "A Pirate Looks at Forty")" (1974); "[Cheeseburger in Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheeseburger_in_Paradise_(song) "Cheeseburger in Paradise (song)")" (1978); "[Why Don't We Get Drunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Don't_We_Get_Drunk "Why Don't We Get Drunk")" (1973); and "[Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changes_in_Latitudes,_Changes_in_Attitudes_(song) "Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes (song)")" (1977). His other popular songs include "[Son of a Son of a Sailor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_of_a_Son_of_a_Sailor_(song) "Son of a Son of a Sailor (song)")" (1978), "[One Particular Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Particular_Harbour_(song) "One Particular Harbour (song)")" (1983), and "[It's Five O'Clock Somewhere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Five_O'Clock_Somewhere "It's Five O'Clock Somewhere")" with [Alan Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Jackson "Alan Jackson") (2003).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-15) Buffett formed the [Coral Reefer Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_Reefer_Band "Coral Reefer Band") in 1975.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-wife-16)

Of over 30 albums released by Buffett, eight are [certified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") gold and nine others are certified platinum or multi-platinum by the RIAA.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-riaa-17) He sold over 20 million certified records worldwide.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-mayor-4)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-20) In addition to two [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") nominations, Buffett was posthumously inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") in [Cleveland, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland") in the Musical Excellence category in 2024.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-hofgreene-21)

Buffett parlayed the "island escapism" lifestyle of his music into several business ventures including the [Jimmy Buffett's Margaritaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett's_Margaritaville "Jimmy Buffett's Margaritaville") restaurant chain, the [Cheeseburger in Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheeseburger_in_Paradise_(restaurant) "Cheeseburger in Paradise (restaurant)") restaurant chain which is defunct, and ventures in hotels, casinos, liquor, and retirement communities. He was a bestselling author. Buffett's estate was estimated to be worth $275 million.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-trusts-22) His devoted fans are known as "Parrotheads".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-state-23)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Buffett was born on December 25, 1946, in [Pascagoula, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pascagoula,_Mississippi "Pascagoula, Mississippi")[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-24) and lived for part of his childhood in [Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile,_Alabama "Mobile, Alabama") and [Fairhope, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairhope,_Alabama "Fairhope, Alabama"). He was the son of Mary Lorraine ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Peets; died September 25, 2003)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-25) and James Delaney Buffett Jr. (died May 1, 2003), who worked for the [United States Army Corps of Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Corps_of_Engineers "United States Army Corps of Engineers").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Icon-28) He had two younger sisters, Laurie (born 1948) and Lucy (born 1953).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-NYTObit-12)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-29) As a child, he was exposed to sailing: his grandfather, James Delaney Buffett, was a [steamship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steamship "Steamship") captain from [Newfoundland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland_Colony "Newfoundland Colony"), and his father was a marine engineer and sailor—these experiences later influenced his music.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-onboard-30)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Icon-28) He was educated by [Jesuits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesuits "Jesuits") as a [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_the_United_States "Catholic Church in the United States") and served as an [altar boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altar_boy "Altar boy").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Catholic-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-words-32)

In 1961, after seeing a folk music ensemble perform in [Biloxi, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biloxi,_Mississippi "Biloxi, Mississippi"), Buffett realized that he wanted to be a musician.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-words-32) His first performance was a month later at a [hootenanny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hootenanny "Hootenanny"), where he played a [Stella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stella_(guitar) "Stella (guitar)") guitar.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-words-32) He attended St. Ignatius Catholic School in Mobile, where he played the [trombone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trombone "Trombone") in the school band at eight in the 1950s.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-33) He graduated from [McGill Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McGill-Toolen_Catholic_High_School "McGill-Toolen Catholic High School") (a high school) in the city in 1964.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Tuscaloosa-35)

Buffett enrolled at [Auburn University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_University "Auburn University") in [Auburn, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn,_Alabama "Auburn, Alabama") and was taught how to play guitar by a [Sigma Pi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigma_Pi "Sigma Pi") fraternity brother to "garner attention from girls".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Icon-28)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Tuscaloosa-35) He flunked out of Auburn after a year, in April 1966, "unable to balance his newfound interests in music and girls with his college classes".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-36) In 1966, Buffett played [acid rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acid_rock "Acid rock") in a band called the Upstairs Alliance which attempted to emulate the sound of [Jefferson Airplane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Airplane "Jefferson Airplane").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-words-32) He continued college at [Pearl River Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_River_Community_College "Pearl River Community College") in [Poplarville, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poplarville,_Mississippi "Poplarville, Mississippi") and the [University of Southern Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_Mississippi "University of Southern Mississippi") in [Hattiesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hattiesburg,_Mississippi "Hattiesburg, Mississippi") and earned a bachelor's degree in history in 1969, where during his time there he also joined the [Kappa Sigma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kappa_Sigma "Kappa Sigma") fraternity. In college, Buffett worked in a shipyard as an electrician and welder.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-onboard-30) He avoided serving in the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War") due to a college deferment, and a failed physical exam.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-rockin-37)

## Music career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music career")]

After graduating in 1969, Buffett moved to [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") and often held [street performances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_performance "Street performance") for tourists on [Decatur Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decatur_Street_(New_Orleans) "Decatur Street (New Orleans)"). Additionally, he played for drunken crowds in the former Bayou Room nightclub on [Bourbon Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbon_Street "Bourbon Street").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-38)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-NYTObit-12) In 1970, he moved to [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee") to further his [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") career. Buffett did not have much luck with music jobs but found work as an editorial assistant for _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_, where he was the first to report that the bluegrass duo [Flatt and Scruggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flatt_and_Scruggs "Flatt and Scruggs") had disbanded.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-bbobit-39)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-NYTObit-12)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-words-32) He signed a two-album contract with [Barnaby Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnaby_Records "Barnaby Records").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-deadat-40) He released his first album, the country-tinged [folk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_rock "Folk rock") record _[Down to Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down\_to\_Earth\_(Jimmy\_Buffett\_album) "Down to Earth (Jimmy Buffett album)"),_ in August 1970; it sold 324 copies.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-NYTObit-12) The masters of his second album, _[High Cumberland Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Cumberland\_Jubilee "High Cumberland Jubilee")_, were recorded in 1971 in [Berry Hill, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berry_Hill,_Tennessee "Berry Hill, Tennessee"). They were allegedly lost by the label before the album was released, although they were found in 1976, after Buffett became popular.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-deadat-40)

In the fall of 1971, after an impromptu audition, Buffett was hired by the Exit/In, a Nashville club, as the [opening act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_act "Opening act") for recording artist Dianne Davidson. Unhappy with the business climate in Nashville and with his first marriage heading for divorce, Buffett accepted an offer by fellow country singer [Jerry Jeff Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Jeff_Walker "Jerry Jeff Walker"), whom he had met while working as a journalist in Nashville, for lodging in his house in [Coconut Grove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut_Grove "Coconut Grove"). In November 1971, they went to [Key West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_West "Key West") on a [busking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busking "Busking") expedition; Buffett liked it so much that he moved there in the spring of 1972.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-mayor-4)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-41) There, Buffett got involved in the literary scene, meeting writers [Thomas McGuane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_McGuane "Thomas McGuane") (who married Buffett's sister[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-rockin-37)), [Jim Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Harrison "Jim Harrison"), [Tom Corcoran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Corcoran_(writer) "Tom Corcoran (writer)"), and [Truman Capote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truman_Capote "Truman Capote");[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-mayor-4) sex and drugs were plentiful.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-42) Buffett was hired by [David Wolkowsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Wolkowsky "David Wolkowsky"), playing for drinks at the Chart Room Bar in the Pier House Motel.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-43) There, Buffett met his second wife.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-wife-16) From a connection he made there, Buffett was hired as the first mate on the yacht of industrialist Foster Talge, heir to [The Rival Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rival_Company "The Rival Company"), which became his day job.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-44)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-45) In 1973, Buffett signed a [recording contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_contract "Recording contract") with [ABC/Dunhill Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Records "ABC Records"), then run by [Don Gant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Gant "Don Gant"). After [Jim Croce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Croce "Jim Croce") died in a plane crash in September 1973, Dunhill promoted Buffett as a replacement.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-46)

Buffett's second release and his first on ABC/Dunhill was _[A White Sport Coat and a Pink Crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_White\_Sport\_Coat\_and\_a\_Pink\_Crustacean "A White Sport Coat and a Pink Crustacean")_, recorded at [Tompall Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tompall_Glaser "Tompall Glaser")'s [Glaser Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glaser_Sound_Studios "Glaser Sound Studios") recording studio on [Music Row](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Row "Music Row") and released in June 1973.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-exitin-47) The album featured the hit singles "[Grapefruit—Juicy Fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grapefruit%E2%80%94Juicy_Fruit "Grapefruit—Juicy Fruit")" and "[Why Don't We Get Drunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Don't_We_Get_Drunk "Why Don't We Get Drunk")" as well as "I Have Found Me a Home", written about his experiences in Key West.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-exitin-47) Buffett used the money he made from the album to buy his first boat.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-onboard-30)_[Living & Dying in 3/4 Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living\_&\_Dying\_in\_3/4\_Time "Living & Dying in 3/4 Time")_, recorded in October 1973 and released in February 1974, deviated from the island-theme of Buffett's other albums. It included "[Come Monday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Monday "Come Monday")", written for his then-girlfriend and future wife,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-wife-16) his first single to place on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). _[A1A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A1A\_(album) "A1A (album)")_, released in December 1974, included "[A Pirate Looks at Forty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Pirate_Looks_at_Forty "A Pirate Looks at Forty")", written about a drug smuggler. In 1975, Buffett formed the [Coral Reefer Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_Reefer_Band "Coral Reefer Band").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-wife-16) He credits his future wife for cleaning up their look, replacing their ripped [Levi jeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levi_Strauss_&_Co. "Levi Strauss & Co.") and collarless shirts.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-wife-16) The band was the [opening act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_act "Opening act") for [the Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagles_(band) "Eagles (band)") in August 1975.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-eagles-48)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Jimmy_Buffett_at_Clemson_%28Taps_1977%29.png/250px-Jimmy_Buffett_at_Clemson_%28Taps_1977%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jimmy_Buffett_at_Clemson_(Taps_1977).png)

Buffett performing at [Clemson University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemson_University "Clemson University") in 1977

_[Havana Daydreamin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana\_Daydreamin' "Havana Daydreamin'")_, produced by [Don Gant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Gant "Don Gant"), was released in January 1976. In January 1977, Buffett released _[Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changes\_in\_Latitudes,\_Changes\_in\_Attitudes "Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes")_, which, in addition to the [title track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changes_in_Latitudes,_Changes_in_Attitudes_(song) "Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes (song)"), featured his breakthrough hit song "[Margaritaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaritaville "Margaritaville")".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-exitin-47) Buffett claims that he wrote most of the song in six minutes.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-mayor-4) Ironically, while it attempts to negatively portray tourists in Key West, it led to an increase in tourism to the city.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-rsobit-49) That year, Buffett sublet his apartment in Key West to [Hunter S. Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_S._Thompson "Hunter S. Thompson").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-rsobit-49)

Buffett first traveled to [Saint Barthélemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Barth%C3%A9lemy "Saint Barthélemy") in 1978[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-onboard-30) and moved there shortly thereafter, where he got the inspiration for songs and characters in his books.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-forward-50) In March 1978, Buffett released _[Son of a Son of a Sailor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son\_of\_a\_Son\_of\_a\_Sailor "Son of a Son of a Sailor")_. In addition to the [title track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_of_a_Son_of_a_Sailor_(song) "Son of a Son of a Sailor (song)"), it featured "[Cheeseburger in Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheeseburger_in_Paradise_(song) "Cheeseburger in Paradise (song)")", which reached number 32 on the Hot 100.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-bbobit-39) In August 1979, he released _[Volcano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcano\_(Jimmy\_Buffett\_album) "Volcano (Jimmy Buffett album)")_, which included "[Fins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fins_(song) "Fins (song)")" and the [title track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcano_(Jimmy_Buffett_song) "Volcano (Jimmy Buffett song)").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-51)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Jimmy_Buffett_1980.jpg/250px-Jimmy_Buffett_1980.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jimmy_Buffett_1980.jpg)

Buffett in 1980

In 1983, Buffett filed and won a lawsuit against [Chi-Chi's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chi-Chi's "Chi-Chi's") for attempting to trademark "Margaritaville" as a drink special.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-52) In October 1985, he released the [compilation album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilation_album "Compilation album")_[Songs You Know By Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songs\_You\_Know\_By\_Heart "Songs You Know By Heart")_, which included all of the "Big Eight" songs and was his best-selling album, selling over 7 million copies by 2005.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-riaa-17) In 1994, Buffett duetted with [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra") on a cover of "[Mack the Knife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mack_the_Knife "Mack the Knife")" on Sinatra's final studio album, _[Duets II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duets\_II\_(Frank\_Sinatra\_album) "Duets II (Frank Sinatra album)")_.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-53) In 1996, Buffett penned the song "Jamaica Mistaica" for his _Banana Wind_ album based on a January 1996 incident in which Buffett's [Grumman HU-16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grumman_HU-16 "Grumman HU-16") airplane named _[Hemisphere Dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemisphere\_Dancer "Hemisphere Dancer")_ was shot at by Jamaican police, who believed the craft to be smuggling marijuana.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-sprayed-54) The aircraft sustained minimal damage. The plane was carrying Buffett as well as [Bono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bono "Bono") of [U2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U2 "U2"), Bono's wife and two children, [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records") producer [Chris Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Blackwell "Chris Blackwell"), and co-pilot Bill Dindy. The [Jamaican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica "Jamaica") government acknowledged the mistake and apologized to Buffett.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-sprayed-54)

In April 1998, Buffett released an album of songs from a [musical theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theatre "Musical theatre") production he co-created based on [Herman Wouk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Wouk "Herman Wouk")'s novel, _[Don't Stop the Carnival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Stop\_the\_Carnival\_(novel) "Don't Stop the Carnival (novel)")_; the album was certified gold.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-riaa-17) After [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra") died the following month, he attended his funeral. Buffett's song "[Math Suks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Math_Suks "Math Suks")", released in May 1999, was condemned by the U.S. [National Council of Teachers of Mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Council_of_Teachers_of_Mathematics "National Council of Teachers of Mathematics") and the [National Education Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Education_Association "National Education Association") for its alleged negative effect on children's education.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-55) Comedian [Jon Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Stewart "Jon Stewart") also jokingly criticized the song on _[The Daily Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Show "The Daily Show")_ during a segment called "Math Is Quite Pleasant".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-56)

By 1999, Buffett had shifted to a more relaxed concert schedule of around 20–30 dates per year, with infrequent back-to-back nights, preferring to play only on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays. This schedule provided the title of his [1999 live album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffett_Live:_Tuesdays,_Thursdays,_Saturdays "Buffett Live: Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-57) In 2003, Buffett partnered in a partial [duet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duet "Duet") with [Alan Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Jackson "Alan Jackson") for the song "[It's Five O'Clock Somewhere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Five_O'Clock_Somewhere "It's Five O'Clock Somewhere")", which spent a then record eight weeks atop the [Hot Country Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs") charts.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-58)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-59) This song won the 2003 [Country Music Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Association "Country Music Association") Award for Vocal Event of the Year, Buffett's first award in his 30-year recording career.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-60) Buffett's album _[License to Chill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/License\_to\_Chill "License to Chill")_, released on July 13, 2004, sold 238,500 copies in its first week of release according to [Nielsen Soundscan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Soundscan "Nielsen Soundscan"). With the album, Buffett topped the U.S. pop albums chart for the first time in his career.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-61)

In May 2005, Buffett signed an agreement with [Sirius Satellite Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sirius_Satellite_Radio "Sirius Satellite Radio") to broadcast [Radio Margaritaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Margaritaville "Radio Margaritaville"), which, from its founding in 1998, was broadcast only online.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-62)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-63) The channel broadcasts from the Margaritaville Resort Orlando in [Kissimmee, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kissimmee,_Florida "Kissimmee, Florida"). In August 2006, Buffett released the album _[Take the Weather with You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take\_the\_Weather\_with\_You "Take the Weather with You")_, which hit number 1 on the country chart.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-64) The album included "Breathe In, Breathe Out, Move On", written in honor of the survivors of [Hurricane Katrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Katrina "Hurricane Katrina").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-beaches-65) In August 2007, Buffett was nominated at the [Country Music Association Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Association_Awards "Country Music Association Awards") for the Event of the Year Award for his song "Hey Good Lookin'" which also features Alan Jackson and [George Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Strait "George Strait").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-66) Also in August 2007, Buffett received a star on the Mohegan Sun Walk of Fame.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-67)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Jimmy_Buffett_1.jpg/250px-Jimmy_Buffett_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jimmy_Buffett_1.jpg)

Buffett performing in January 2008

In April 2010, a double CD of performances recorded during the 2008 and 2009 tours called _[Encores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encores\_(Jimmy\_Buffett\_album) "Encores (Jimmy Buffett album)")_ was released exclusively at [Walmart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walmart "Walmart"), Walmart.com, and Margaritaville.com.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-68) In 2010, Buffett was named the tenth biggest touring artist of the decade, with 4.5 million ticket sales over the previous 10 years.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-rsobit-49) Since [Wyatt Durrette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyatt_Durrette_(songwriter) "Wyatt Durrette (songwriter)"), co-writer of the song "[Knee Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee_Deep "Knee Deep")", was a fan of Buffett's, Buffett partnered on the song with the [Zac Brown Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zac_Brown_Band "Zac Brown Band"), which was released on Brown's 2010 album _[You Get What You Give](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You\_Get\_What\_You\_Give\_(album) "You Get What You Give (album)")_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-69) The single was certified platinum in September 2017.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-riaa-17)

In November 2011, Buffett voiced [Huckleberry Finn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huckleberry_Finn "Huckleberry Finn") on _[Mark Twain: Words & Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark\_Twain:\_Words\_&\_Music "Mark Twain: Words & Music")_, a benefit for the [Mark Twain Boyhood Home & Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Twain_Boyhood_Home_&_Museum "Mark Twain Boyhood Home & Museum"), which was released on [Mailboat Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mailboat_Records "Mailboat Records").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-70) In August 2013, Buffett released _[Songs from St. Somewhere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songs\_from\_St.\_Somewhere "Songs from St. Somewhere")_; many of the songs were recorded at [Eden Rock, St Barths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Rock,_St_Barths "Eden Rock, St Barths").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-forward-50)

In 2020, Buffett released _Songs You Don't Know by Heart_, a fan-curated collection of his lesser-known songs rerecorded on his collection of notable guitars.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-71) Buffett performed his final full concert at [Snapdragon Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapdragon_Stadium "Snapdragon Stadium") in [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego") on May 6, 2023.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-final-72) He made two further concert appearances, as an unannounced guest at concerts by Coral Reefer Band members, in [Amagansett, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amagansett,_New_York "Amagansett, New York"), on June 11 and in [Portsmouth, Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth,_Rhode_Island "Portsmouth, Rhode Island"), on July 2, his final live performance before his death.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-final-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-73)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-74)_[Equal Strain on All Parts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equal\_Strain\_on\_All\_Parts "Equal Strain on All Parts")_ was released posthumously in November 2023. Buffett got the idea for the album title from his grandfather's description of a nap.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-75)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-76) Buffett was posthumously selected for induction into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") in 2024 in the musical excellence category.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-rrhof24-77)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-hofgreene-21)

### Musical style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Musical style")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/37/Mac_mcanally_and_jimmy_buffett.jpg/250px-Mac_mcanally_and_jimmy_buffett.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mac_mcanally_and_jimmy_buffett.jpg)

Buffett _(right)_ performing in 2009

Buffett's music combined country, [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"), [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_folk_music "American folk music"), [calypso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calypso_music "Calypso music"), and [pop music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") with coastal as well as tropical lyrical themes for a sound sometimes called "gulf and western”.

Buffett said his music is "drunken Caribbean rock 'n' roll".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-78) He has also described his music as follows:

> It's pure escapism is all it is...I'm not the first one to do it, nor shall I probably be the last. But I think it's really a part of the human condition that you've got to have some fun. You've got to get away from whatever you do to make a living or other parts of life that stress you out. I try to make it at least 50/50 fun to work and so far it's worked out.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-79)

In 1989, a music critic in _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ described Buffett's music as a combination of "tropical languor with country funkiness into what some [have] called the Key West sound, or Gulf-and-western."[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-80) The name "Gulf-and-western" derives from elements in Buffett's early music including musical influence from [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"), along with lyrical themes from the coast of the [Gulf of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico"). It is a play on the form of "Country & Western" and [Gulf+Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf+Western "Gulf+Western") is the former parent company of [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures").

In 2020, The [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") described Buffett's sound as a "special [Gulf Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coast_of_the_United_States "Gulf Coast of the United States") blend of country, [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"), [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_folk_music "American folk music") and rock, topped by Buffett's swaying voice. Few can mix [steelpans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steelpan "Steelpan"), [trombones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trombone "Trombone") and [pedal steel guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedal_steel_guitar "Pedal steel guitar") so effortlessly."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-81)

### Musical legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Musical legacy")]

Musicians that have cited Buffett as a musical influence include [Greg "Fingers" Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_%22Fingers%22_Taylor "Greg \"Fingers\" Taylor"), a former member of Buffett's [Coral Reefer Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_Reefer_Band "Coral Reefer Band"), as well as musicians that have "latched on to his seaside-and-booze themes" such as [Kenny Chesney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Chesney "Kenny Chesney"), [Alan Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Jackson "Alan Jackson"), and [Zac Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zac_Brown "Zac Brown").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-beaches-65)

### "Parrot Head" fans

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: \"Parrot Head\" fans")]

**Parrot Head** or **parrothead** is a commonly used nickname for Buffett fans, with "parakeets" or "keets" used for younger fans, or children of Parrotheads. At a 1985 Jimmy Buffett concert at the Timberwolf Amphitheater at [Kings Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_Island "Kings Island") in [Mason, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason,_Ohio "Mason, Ohio"), Buffett commented about everyone wearing Hawaiian shirts and parrot hats and how they kept coming back to see his shows, just like [Deadheads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadheads "Deadheads"). [Timothy B. Schmit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_B._Schmit "Timothy B. Schmit"), then a member of the [Coral Reefer Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_Reefer_Band "Coral Reefer Band"), coined the term "Parrot Head" to describe them.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-82)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-83) In 1989, the first Parrothead club was founded in [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-84) The annual Meeting of the Minds in [Key West, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_West,_Florida "Key West, Florida") is a five-day festival held after [Fantasy Fest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_Fest "Fantasy Fest") that attracts approximately 5,000 Parrotheads.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-85) The Pikes Peak Hash House Harriers and Harriettes have an annual Parrot Head Hash weekend hosted by Yeastee Boy and Bread Box. Buffett's fanbase is composed mostly of [baby boomers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_boomers "Baby boomers").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-state-23) His concerts were known for [tailgate parties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tailgate_parties "Tailgate parties") and alcohol consumption.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-mayor-4)

## Writing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Writing")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Jimmy_Buffett_navy_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Jimmy_Buffett_navy_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jimmy_Buffett_navy_(cropped).jpg)

Buffett in Hawaii in June 2003

Buffett wrote three books, all of which placed on [The New York Times Best Seller list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Best_Seller_list "The New York Times Best Seller list"). _[Tales from Margaritaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tales\_from\_Margaritaville "Tales from Margaritaville")_ and _[Where Is Joe Merchant?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where\_Is\_Joe\_Merchant%3F "Where Is Joe Merchant?")_ both spent over seven months on [_The New York Times_ Best Seller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times_Best_Seller_list "The New York Times Best Seller list") fiction list. His memoir _[A Pirate Looks at Fifty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Pirate\_Looks\_at\_Fifty "A Pirate Looks at Fifty"),_ published in 1998, went straight to number one on the _New York Times_ Best Seller nonfiction list, making him one of the few authors to have reached number one on both the fiction and nonfiction lists.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-86)

Buffett also co-wrote two children's books, _[The Jolly Mon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jolly\_Mon "The Jolly Mon")_ and _Trouble Dolls,_ with his eldest daughter, [Savannah Buffett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savannah_Buffett "Savannah Buffett"). The original hardcover release of _The Jolly Mon_ included a cassette tape recording of the two reading the story accompanied by an original score written by [Michael Utley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Utley "Michael Utley").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-87)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-88)

Buffett's novel _[A Salty Piece of Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Salty\_Piece\_of\_Land "A Salty Piece of Land")_ was released on November 30, 2004, and the first edition of the book included a CD single of the song "A Salty Piece of Land." The book was a _New York Times_ best seller soon after its release.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-89)

Buffett's last title, _Swine Not?_, was released on May 13, 2008.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-90)

## Theater

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Theater")]

In 1994, Buffett began developing a musical based on [Herman Wouk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Wouk "Herman Wouk")'s 1965 novel, _[Don't Stop the Carnival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Stop\_the\_Carnival\_(novel) "Don't Stop the Carnival (novel)")_. Buffett wrote the music and lyrics and Wouk wrote the book for the show. _Don't Stop the Carnival_ debuted in [Miami, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami"), in 1997 to negative reviews from critics.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-106) The show ran only for six weeks in Miami.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-107)

_[Escape to Margaritaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escape\_to\_Margaritaville "Escape to Margaritaville")_, a musical, ran at the [La Jolla Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jolla_Playhouse "La Jolla Playhouse") in [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego") from May 2017 to July 2017. The show then performed limited runs in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans"), [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), and [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), and was well received by critics. The show features a book by [Greg Garcia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Garcia_(producer) "Greg Garcia (producer)") and [Mike O'Malley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_O'Malley "Mike O'Malley") and uses Buffett's classic songs, some of which he rewrote the lyrics to in order to better fit in the context of the story. The show began previews at the [Marquis Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquis_Theatre "Marquis Theatre") on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") on February 16, 2018, and officially opened on March 15 under the direction of [Tony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award "Tony Award") winner [Christopher Ashley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Ashley "Christopher Ashley"). The Broadway production received mixed reviews from New York critics and closed on July 1 after 29 previews and 124 regular performances. A national tour launched in [Providence, Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"), in the fall of 2019.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Lifestyle-108)

## Business ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Business ventures")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Margaritaville.JPG/250px-Margaritaville.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Margaritaville.JPG)

The outside of a Margaritaville restaurant in [Orlando, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida")

Buffett took advantage of the [tropical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical "Tropical") "island escapism" lifestyle that fans of his music sought by launching several business ventures to sell this lifestyle to his fans.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-109)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Lifestyle-108) Through his Margaritaville brand, Buffett licensed hotels, casinos, cruise experiences, restaurants and bars, packaged foods, beverages, spirits, outdoor furniture, home goods, appliances, and apparel and accessories.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-110)

### Restaurants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Restaurants")]

In 1984, Buffett and a friend opened a T-shirt shop and expanded it into the first Margaritaville Cafe, in [Gulf Shores, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Shores,_Alabama "Gulf Shores, Alabama").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-rockin-37) After it failed, in 1985, they tried again in Key West, expanding it to what became [Jimmy Buffett's Margaritaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett's_Margaritaville "Jimmy Buffett's Margaritaville") in 1987.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-insideme-3) The chain opened restaurants under the Margaritaville and LandShark Bar & Grill names in locations including Atlantic City, New Orleans, Nashville, the Cayman Islands, The Bahamas, Turks and Caicos, Las Vegas, Jamaica, Orlando, and [Baltimore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore "Baltimore").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-111) The Margaritaville cafe on the Las Vegas strip was possibly the highest grossing restaurant in the U.S.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-112)

Buffett previously owned the [Cheeseburger in Paradise Restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheeseburger_in_Paradise_(restaurant) "Cheeseburger in Paradise (restaurant)") chain, founded in 2002 in partnership with [Bloomin' Brands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomin'_Brands "Bloomin' Brands"); it was sold to [Luby's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luby's "Luby's") for $11 million in 2012 and shut down in 2020.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Steele-113)

### Record labels

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Record labels")]

In 1992, Buffett launched Margaritaville Records, with distribution through [MCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCA_Records "MCA Records").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-114) His MCA record deal ended in 1996. In 1999, he started [Mailboat Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mailboat_Records "Mailboat Records") to release live albums.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-115)

### Beer

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Beer")]

Buffett sought and received a concert sponsorship from [Corona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corona_(beer) "Corona (beer)"); the partnership was credited for increasing sales of the brand.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-mayor-4) After deciding that he wanted his own beer brand, Buffett partnered with [Anheuser-Busch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anheuser-Busch "Anheuser-Busch") in 2006 to brew Landshark Lager, now one of the [Anheuser-Busch brands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anheuser-Busch_brands "Anheuser-Busch brands").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-116)

### Casinos

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Casinos")]

In 2013, Buffett partnered with the [Resorts Casino Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resorts_Casino_Hotel "Resorts Casino Hotel") in [Atlantic City, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_City,_New_Jersey "Atlantic City, New Jersey"), to open the $35 million Jimmy Buffett Margaritaville-themed entertainment complex at the hotel, which included a Margaritaville Restaurant with a giant blender and tiki bar, a Landshark Bar and Grill, the 5 O'Clock Somewhere Bar, a coffee shop, a retail store, and a gaming area with 12 Margaritaville-themed table games and 160 slot machines.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-casino-117)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-cutting-118)

The [Margaritaville Casino and Restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaritaville_Casino_and_Restaurant "Margaritaville Casino and Restaurant") in [Biloxi, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biloxi,_Mississippi "Biloxi, Mississippi"), licensed the name from Buffett; it was in operation from May 2012 to September 2014.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-119) Plans to bring a Buffett-themed casino to Biloxi had been in process since 2000.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-120)

### Sports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Sports")]

From May 8, 2009, through January 5, 2010, the home stadium of the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"), now called [Hard Rock Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_Rock_Stadium "Hard Rock Stadium"), was named LandShark Stadium pursuant to an eight-month naming rights deal.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-121) Buffett also wrote new lyrics for the team to his 1979 song "[Fins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fins_(song) "Fins (song)")", which is played during Dolphins home games.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-122)

### Berkshire Hathaway

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Berkshire Hathaway")]

In the 1980s, Buffett became friends with [Warren Buffett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Buffett "Warren Buffett") and a shareholder in [Berkshire Hathaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkshire_Hathaway "Berkshire Hathaway"), increasing his stake over the years. They called each other "Cousin Jimmy" and "Uncle Warren" though they were not related.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Steele-113)

## Charity work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Charity work")]

### Environmental conservation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Environmental conservation")]

In 1981, the [Save the Manatee Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_the_Manatee_Club "Save the Manatee Club"), a [501(c)(3) organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/501(c)(3)_organization "501(c)(3) organization"), was founded by Buffett and former Florida governor [Bob Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Graham "Bob Graham").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-influence-134)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-135) In 1986, Buffett began work to introduce the "Save the Manatee" [license plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/License_plate "License plate"), featuring an image of a [West Indian manatee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Indian_manatee "West Indian manatee"), with proceeds going to the Save the Manatee Club.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-influence-134) Buffett was also a major donor to the [Gulf Specimen Marine Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Specimen_Marine_Laboratory "Gulf Specimen Marine Laboratory").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-influence-134)

In 1987, Buffett lobbied for the reauthorization of the [Endangered Species Act of 1973](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered_Species_Act_of_1973 "Endangered Species Act of 1973").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-influence-134)

Buffett enjoyed playing for U.S. troops; he played at the [Guantanamo Bay Naval Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guantanamo_Bay_Naval_Base "Guantanamo Bay Naval Base") in 2002.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-136)

After the [2010 Haiti earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Haiti_earthquake "2010 Haiti earthquake"), Buffett brought tents via his seaplane to donate to those that lost their homes.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-145)

In the aftermath of [Hurricane Irma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Irma "Hurricane Irma"), Buffett sent private planes to help ferry supplies and gave a benefit concert in [Gustavia, Saint Barthélemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavia,_Saint_Barth%C3%A9lemy "Gustavia, Saint Barthélemy").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-forward-50)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Buffett married Margie Washichek in 1969; they divorced in 1972.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-146) Buffett met his second wife, Jane (née Slagsvol), then a student at the [University of South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_South_Carolina "University of South Carolina"), at the Chart Room bar while she was visiting Key West on [spring break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_break "Spring break"); she never returned to the university. They were married in 1977 in Aspen, Colorado. [The Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagles_(band) "Eagles (band)"), for whom Buffett was the opening act in 1975, played at their wedding.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-rockin-37)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-eagles-48) The couple had two daughters, radio personality [Savannah Buffett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savannah_Buffett "Savannah Buffett") (born 1979) and filmmaker Sarah Delaney (born 1992), and an adopted son, Cameron Marley (born 1994).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-wife-16)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-whoare-147) They split in the early 1980s due to their partying lifestyle but reconciled in 1991 after she became sober.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-wife-16)

Buffett resided in a waterfront estate in [Sag Harbor, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sag_Harbor,_New_York "Sag Harbor, New York"). In September 1998, he sold his properties in Key West for $900,000.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-148) In 2010, Buffett sold his house in [Palm Beach, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Beach,_Florida "Palm Beach, Florida"), to [Jon Stryker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Stryker "Jon Stryker") for $18.5 million; he had bought the house in 1994 for $4.4 million. At that time, he also owned a 2-unit property in the area, which he purchased in 2002 for $802,000.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-149) In 2013, Buffett purchased another house in Palm Beach, with 3,100 square feet, for $1.3 million.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-150) In April 2014, he bought a 4,322 square foot house in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California") for $8.25 million.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-151) In 2020, Buffett sold a 4,783-square-foot house in Palm Beach for $6.9 million; he paid $4.95 million for it in 2011.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-152) Buffett also owned a home in [Saint Barthélemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Barth%C3%A9lemy "Saint Barthélemy"), where he lived on and off in the early 1980s. There, Buffett was part owner of the Autour de Rocher hotel and restaurant. It was closed by local police and burned down shortly after (the story of the hotel is chronicled in the song "Autour Du Rocher" on Buffett's 2002 _[Far Side of the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far\_Side\_of\_the\_World\_(album) "Far Side of the World (album)")_ album).[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-forward-50) He also owned an apartment in the [Deutsche Bank Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Bank_Center "Deutsche Bank Center") in New York City.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Lifestyle-108)

Buffett was an avid pilot and owned a [Dassault Falcon 900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Falcon_900 "Dassault Falcon 900") jet that he often used while on concert tours and during his travels. At various points, he also owned a [Boeing Stearman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_Stearman "Boeing Stearman"), [Cessna Citation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cessna_Citation "Cessna Citation"), [Lake Amphibian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Amphibian "Lake Amphibian"), [Pilatus PC-12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pilatus_PC-12 "Pilatus PC-12"), and [Grumman Albatross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grumman_Albatross "Grumman Albatross").[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-flies-153) While attempting to take off on August 25, 1994, around 3:00 p.m. Eastern time, Buffett crashed his [Grumman G-44 Widgeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grumman_G-44_Widgeon "Grumman G-44 Widgeon") into the waters off [Nantucket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nantucket "Nantucket"), Massachusetts. The airplane nosed over, and Buffett was able to swim to safety, sustaining only minor injuries.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-154)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-flies-153)

Buffett was raised Catholic, although he did not practice the religion later in life.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Catholic-31)

### Sports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Sports")]

Buffett was a devoted [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") fan, having attended the team's first game at [Tulane Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulane_Stadium "Tulane Stadium") in 1967.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-155) On April 1, 2012, he had Saints head coach [Sean Payton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Payton "Sean Payton") serve as an honorary member of the Coral Reefer Band at a concert in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") in protest of Payton's suspension by the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") as a result of the [New Orleans Saints bounty scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints_bounty_scandal "New Orleans Saints bounty scandal").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-156)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-157)

On February 4, 2001, Buffett was ejected from the American Airlines Arena (now the [Kaseya Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaseya_Center "Kaseya Center")) in Miami during a basketball game between the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") and the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") for cursing.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-158) The referee who ejected Buffett apparently did not know who he was, and got upset at Heat coach [Pat Riley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Riley "Pat Riley") because he thought Riley—who was trying to explain to him who Buffett was—was insulting him by asking if he had ever been a "Parrothead", the nickname for Buffett fans.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-159)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

On October 6, 2006, Buffett was detained by French customs officials in [Saint Tropez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Tropez "Saint Tropez") for allegedly carrying over 100 pills of [ecstasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methylenedioxymethamphetamine "Methylenedioxymethamphetamine"). Buffett's luggage was searched after his [Dassault Falcon 900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Falcon_900 "Dassault Falcon 900") private jet landed at Toulon-Hyères International Airport. He paid a fine of $300 and was released. A [spokesperson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spokesperson "Spokesperson") for Buffett stated the pills in question were [prescription drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prescription_drugs "Prescription drugs") but declined to name the drug or the health problem for which he was being treated. Buffett released a statement that the "ecstasy" was in fact a B-vitamin supplement known as [Foltx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foltx "Foltx").[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-160)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-161)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-162)

### Health

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Health")]

At a performance by Buffett on January 26, 2011 ([Australia Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_Day "Australia Day")) at Sydney's [Hordern Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hordern_Pavilion "Hordern Pavilion"), he fell off the stage after an encore and lost consciousness.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-doingwell-163)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-164) Coincidentally, [Gordian Fulde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordian_Fulde "Gordian Fulde"), a trauma surgeon, was at the concert and close to the stage; Fulde treated Buffett at the scene.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-doingwell-163)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-165)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-166)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-167) Buffett regained consciousness within a few minutes, and was then transported to St. Vincent's Hospital Emergency Centre for treatment and was discharged the next day.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-doingwell-163) Buffett returned to Australia in 2012 for two shows in Brisbane and Melbourne, and made fun of the incident during those shows.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-168)

By 2017, Buffett's diet did not include sugar or [carbohydrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbohydrate "Carbohydrate"), except on Sundays, and he no longer smoked [marijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marijuana "Marijuana").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-Lifestyle-108)

### Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Politics")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/President_Bill_Clinton_greets_musician_Jimmy_Buffett_in_the_Outer_Oval_Office_area.jpg/250px-President_Bill_Clinton_greets_musician_Jimmy_Buffett_in_the_Outer_Oval_Office_area.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Bill_Clinton_greets_musician_Jimmy_Buffett_in_the_Outer_Oval_Office_area.jpg)

Buffett with US President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") in 1993

Buffett was a supporter of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"). He sang in Florida for the [Bill Clinton 1992 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton_1992_presidential_campaign "Bill Clinton 1992 presidential campaign") and again for [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") in the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") in August 2000.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-169) Buffett hosted fundraisers for Democratic politicians, including one for Obama in 2008, several for [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton") in 2016.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-170) In 2018, Buffett hosted a concert to support [Gwen Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Graham "Gwen Graham"), daughter of [Bob Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Graham "Bob Graham"), in the Democratic primary of the [2018 Florida gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Florida_gubernatorial_election "2018 Florida gubernatorial election").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-influence-134) In November 2018, he hosted a rally for Florida Democratic candidates [Andrew Gillum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Gillum "Andrew Gillum") and [Bill Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Nelson "Bill Nelson") in [West Palm Beach, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Palm_Beach,_Florida "West Palm Beach, Florida"), changing the lyrics of some of his songs to disparage the policies of [Rick Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Scott "Rick Scott") and [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"). The rally faced some backlash from conservative fans.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-171)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-172)

### Illness and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Illness and death")]

Buffett was diagnosed with [Merkel-cell carcinoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merkel-cell_carcinoma "Merkel-cell carcinoma"), a rare and aggressive [skin cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin_cancer "Skin cancer"), in 2019, but kept his illness private and continued to tour while undergoing treatment.

In May 2023, Buffett was hospitalized to "address some issues that needed immediate attention" and rescheduled tour dates.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-173) In late August, he entered [hospice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hospice "Hospice") care[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-174) and had a final meeting with family and friends.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-175)

Buffett died on the evening of September 1, 2023, at age 76, at his home in [Sag Harbor, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sag_Harbor,_New_York "Sag Harbor, New York").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-mayor-4)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-bbobit-39) Buffett's estate was estimated to be worth $275 million.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-trusts-22)

President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") called Buffett a "music icon".[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-176) A tribute concert was held at the [Hollywood Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Bowl "Hollywood Bowl") in April 2024, featuring [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney"), [Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagles_(band) "Eagles (band)"), [Snoop Dogg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snoop_Dogg "Snoop Dogg"), [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford"), and [Pitbull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitbull_(rapper) "Pitbull (rapper)") among others.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-177)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-178)

In 2025, Buffett's widow, Jane Buffett, sued her co-trustee of the trust that owned her husband's assets for mismanagement.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-trusts-22)

## Honors

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jimmy_Buffett&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Honors")]

In 2015, Buffett spoke at the [University of Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Miami "University of Miami")'s graduation ceremony and received an honorary doctorate in music. Wearing aviator sunglasses, he told graduates, from a line in his song "The Pascagoula Run", that "it's time to see the world, time to kiss a girl, and time to cross the wild meridian."[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-179) Also in 2015, Buffett's hometown of [Pascagoula, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pascagoula,_Mississippi "Pascagoula, Mississippi") named a bridge in his honor, Buffett Bridge.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-180)

A species of [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean "Crustacean") discovered in 2023, _[Gnathia jimmybuffetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gnathia\_jimmybuffetti "Gnathia jimmybuffetti")_, was named after Buffett.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-181)

In 2024, the Florida legislature declared August 30 **Jimmy Buffett Day**, renamed [State Road A1A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Road_A1A "State Road A1A") as the **Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway**, and issued a commemorative Florida and Margaritaville-themed license plate, to benefit Buffett's charity SFC Charitable Foundation Inc., also known as Singing for Change.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-182)

The City of [Hattiesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hattiesburg "Hattiesburg") unveiled their 57th mural in October 2024, titled "Parrots in Paradise." The mural is on Hardy Street and was painted by [Gulfport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulfport,_Mississippi "Gulfport, Mississippi") artist Lucinda L'Enfant.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-183)

In 2024, Jimmy Buffett was posthumously inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame"). The honor was bestowed by [James Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Taylor "James Taylor"), who also sang Buffett's 1974 hit "Come Monday" along with [Kenny Chesney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Chesney "Kenny Chesney") and [Coral Reefer Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_Reefer_Band "Coral Reefer Band") member [Mac McAnally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_McAnally "Mac McAnally"). [Dave Matthews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Matthews "Dave Matthews") also performed "A Pirate Looks at Forty".

In 2025, Florida Governor [Ron DeSantis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_DeSantis "Ron DeSantis") posthumously awarded Buffett the Florida Governor's Medal of Freedom, one of the highest civilian honors in the state.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Buffett#cite_note-184)

**Randy Bruce Traywick** (born May 4, 1959), known professionally as **Randy Travis**, is an American [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") and [gospel music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_music "Gospel music") singer and songwriter, as well as a film and television actor. Active since 1979, he has recorded over 20 studio albums and charted more than 50 singles on _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s [Hot Country Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs") charts, including sixteen that reached the number-one position.

Travis's commercial success began in the mid-1980s with the release of his album _[Storms of Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storms\_of\_Life "Storms of Life")_, which was certified triple-platinum by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America"). He followed up his major-label debut with a string of platinum and multi-platinum albums, but his commercial success declined throughout the 1990s. In 1997, he left [Warner Bros. Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Records "Warner Bros. Records") for [DreamWorks Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DreamWorks_Records "DreamWorks Records"); he signed to [Word Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_Records "Word Records") for a series of gospel albums beginning in 2000 before transferring back to Warner at the end of the 21st century's first decade. His musical accolades include seven [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), eleven [ACM Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Country_Music "Academy of Country Music"), eight [Dove Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dove_Awards "Dove Awards"), a star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame"), and a 2016 induction into the [Country Music Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Hall_of_Fame "Country Music Hall of Fame"). Major songs of his include "[On the Other Hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_the_Other_Hand "On the Other Hand")", "[Forever and Ever, Amen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forever_and_Ever,_Amen "Forever and Ever, Amen")", "[I Told You So](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Told_You_So_(Randy_Travis_song) "I Told You So (Randy Travis song)")", "[Hard Rock Bottom of Your Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_Rock_Bottom_of_Your_Heart "Hard Rock Bottom of Your Heart")", and "[Three Wooden Crosses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Wooden_Crosses "Three Wooden Crosses")".

He is noted as a key figure in the [neotraditional country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neotraditional_country "Neotraditional country") movement, a return to more traditional sounds within the genre following the [country pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_pop "Country pop") crossovers of the early 1980s. Nearly all of his albums were produced or co-produced by [Kyle Lehning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Lehning "Kyle Lehning"), and feature frequent co-writing credits from [Paul Overstreet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Overstreet "Paul Overstreet"), [Don Schlitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Schlitz "Don Schlitz"), and [Skip Ewing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skip_Ewing "Skip Ewing"). Critics have compared his [baritone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baritone "Baritone") singing voice to other artists such as [Lefty Frizzell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lefty_Frizzell "Lefty Frizzell"), [Merle Haggard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merle_Haggard "Merle Haggard"), and [George Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Jones "George Jones"). Since surviving a near-fatal [stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stroke "Stroke") in 2013, which severely limited his singing and speaking ability, he has released archival recordings and made limited public appearances. James Dupré has toured singing Travis's songs with his road band. Between mid-2024 and January 2025, Travis released two new songs where his voice was re-created via [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence").

Travis's acting career includes roles in the television movies _[Wind in the Wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind\_in\_the\_Wire\_(film) "Wind in the Wire (film)")_ (1993) and _[A Holiday to Remember](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Holiday\_to\_Remember "A Holiday to Remember")_ (1995), as well as the [Patrick Swayze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Swayze "Patrick Swayze") movie _[Black Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Dog\_(1998\_film) "Black Dog (1998 film)")_ (1998).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Randy_Travis&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Randy Bruce Traywick was born May 4, 1959, in [Marshville, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshville,_North_Carolina "Marshville, North Carolina").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Travis#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhitburn2017365,_366-1) He is the second of six children to Bobbie and Harold Traywick.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Travis#cite_note-FOOTNOTECusic19901%E2%80%933,_8,_9-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Travis#cite_note-FOOTNOTETravisAbraham20193,_4-3) Harold Traywick worked as a meat packer and also built houses.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Travis#cite_note-FOOTNOTECusic19908,_9-4) He also enjoyed listening to [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") such as [Ernest Tubb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_Tubb "Ernest Tubb") and [Patsy Cline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patsy_Cline "Patsy Cline"), in addition to singing, playing guitar, and writing his own songs. By the time Randy was eight years old, his father sent him and his brothers, Ricky and David, to the house of a friend named Kate Magnum, who taught them how to play guitar.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Travis#cite_note-FOOTNOTECusic199012-5) Harold also constructed a stage behind the family house, where he invited friends over to hear his sons sing.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Travis#cite_note-FOOTNOTECusic199013-6) Randy and Ricky performed publicly for the first time in 1968 at a talent show held at the local [elementary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_school "Elementary school"); while the brothers did not win, they continued to perform at local talent shows, with David later joining to accompany them on [bass guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_guitar "Bass guitar").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Travis#cite_note-FOOTNOTECusic199013,_14-7)
