August 2015, he signed a [recording contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_contract "Recording contract") with [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Schwartz2015-7)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-48) Malone went on to work with a number of prominent rappers including [50 Cent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50_Cent "50 Cent"), [Young Thug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Thug "Young Thug"), [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") and others.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-50) In August 2015, he performed at [Kylie Jenner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylie_Jenner "Kylie Jenner")'s 18th birthday party,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-51) where he met Kanye West, who enjoyed his music, "Jimmy Kimmel Live!")_, performing "Go Flex".[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-57)

In June 2016, [_XXL_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XXL_(magazine) "XXL (magazine)") editor-in-chief Vanessa Satten revealed Malone was considered for _XXL_'s "2016 Freshman Class" magazine cover, but she was "told by his camp that he wasn't paying attention to hip hop so much. He was going in more of a [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music")/[pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music")/[country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") direction."[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-58) However, Malone denied these claims, explaining that his latest mixtape as well as his upcoming album were both hip-hop.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-59) In August 2016, Malone issued an apology for his album, _[Stoney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoney\_(album) "Stoney (album)")_, being late.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-60) It was available for pre-order on November 4, and was finally released on December 13. ### 2017–2019: _Beerbongs & Bentleys_ and _Hollywood's Bleeding_

Main articles: [_Beerbongs & Bentleys_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beerbongs_&_Bentleys "Beerbongs & Bentleys") and [_Hollywood's Bleeding_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood's_Bleeding "Hollywood's Bleeding")

In February 2017, Malone revealed the title of his next project, _[Beerbongs & Bentleys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beerbongs\_&\_Bentleys "Beerbongs & Bentleys")_,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-64) and was set to be released in December, before eventually being pushed back to 2018.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-65) In September, Malone released the first single from the album, "[Rockstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockstar_(Post_Malone_song) "Rockstar (Post Malone song)")" (featuring [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage")). The song peaked at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and held the spot for eight consecutive weeks[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-66) prompting _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ in 2017 to say he is "one of the most popular musicians in the country". In November of the same year, Malone released the official music video for "Rockstar", directed by [Emil Nava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Nava "Emil Nava").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-70)

On February 20, 2018, Malone previewed his new song with [Ty Dolla Sign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Dolla_Sign "Ty Dolla Sign") titled "[Psycho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psycho_(Post_Malone_song) "Psycho (Post Malone song)")".[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-71) "Psycho" was released on February 23, 2018,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-72) and a tour with 21 Savage was announced.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-73) The song debuted at number 2 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, becoming Malone's third entry in the top 10; it would later top the charts in June of that year, becoming Malone's second number one.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-74) On April 5, 2018, Malone stated that _Beerbongs & Bentleys_ will be released on April 27, 2018.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-75) The same day, he also premiered the song "Stay" during the Bud Lite Dive Bar show in Nashville.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-76) Upon release, _Beerbongs & Bentleys_ broke the first day streaming records on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), with 78.7 million streams worldwide.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-77) It debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200 moving 461,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") in its first week, with 153,000 coming from pure sales. The album was also certified platinum by the RIAA after four days[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-78) and spawned three top 10 songs and six top 20 songs.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-79)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Post_Malone_Stavernfestivalen_2018_%28202128%29.jpg/250px-Post_Malone_Stavernfestivalen_2018_%28202128%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Post_Malone_Stavernfestivalen_2018_(202128).jpg)

Malone performing on the main stage at [Stavernfestivalen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stavernfestivalen "Stavernfestivalen") in [Stavern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stavern "Stavern"), Norway in 2018

In an interview with _Billboard_ in May 2018, Malone's manager announced that Malone was planning to start his own record label and film production company[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-80) and Malone later won Top Rap Song at the _Billboard_ Music Awards for "Rockstar".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-81) Malone confirmed in June 2018 that he was writing his third album,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-82) and confirmed that a festival would be taking place, organized by him, titled "Posty Fest", in Dallas, Texas on October 28. Malone promised a "blockbuster" lineup with headliners like rapper [Travis Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Scott "Travis Scott").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-83)

In August, Malone broke [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson")'s 34-year-old record for most weeks on _Billboard_'s Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart, with _Stoney_ reaching its 77th week on the ranking compared to the 76 weeks that _[Thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller\_(Michael\_Jackson\_album) "Thriller (Michael Jackson album)")_ (1983) spent.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:7-84) A collaboration album with rapper [Mac Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Miller "Mac Miller") was also teased in August 2018.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-85) During his appearance on _[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Jimmy\_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")_, he previewed his song "[Sunflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_(Post_Malone_and_Swae_Lee_song) "Sunflower (Post Malone and Swae Lee song)")", a collaboration with [Swae Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swae_Lee "Swae Lee"), from the soundtrack to the film _[Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Into\_the\_Spider-Verse "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse")_.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-87) In November 2018, it was confirmed Malone was recording his third album in his Utah home.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Us_Weekly-88)

Malone was nominated for four awards at the [61st Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Grammy_Awards "61st Grammy Awards") for his album _Beerbongs & Bentleys_. Among the nominations were [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") and [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year"). He performed with the [Red Hot Chili Peppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hot_Chili_Peppers "Red Hot Chili Peppers") at the awards show on February 10, 2019.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-90) In July 2019, Malone released the single "[Goodbyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbyes_(Post_Malone_song) "Goodbyes (Post Malone song)")" (featuring [Young Thug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Thug "Young Thug")), and also announced the [Runaway Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runaway_Tour_(Post_Malone_tour) "Runaway Tour (Post Malone tour)") with Swae Lee as the opener.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-91) On August 5, Malone shared a snippet of an unreleased track, "[Circles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circles_(Post_Malone_song) "Circles (Post Malone song)")", on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"). He then performed the song at his second annual _Bud Light: Dive Bar_ concert and confirmed that the official song would be released the following week.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-92) That same day and on July 25, 2019, at [Cheyenne Frontier Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Frontier_Days "Cheyenne Frontier Days") he announced the album was finished.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-93) He released the song on August 30, 2019.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Aniftos-94) He confirmed that his third studio album would be released on September 6, 2019.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-96) On August 26, 2019, Malone announced on [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") that his third album is called _[Hollywood's Bleeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood's\_Bleeding "Hollywood's Bleeding")_ and would be released on September 6, 2019.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-97)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Aniftos-94) The album debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200, selling 489,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") in its first week.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-98)_Hollywood's Bleeding_ would also be nominated for [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") at the [63rd Grammys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/63rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "63rd Annual Grammy Awards").

### 2020–2022: Collaborations, hiatus, and _Twelve Carat Toothache_

Main article: [_Twelve Carat Toothache_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve_Carat_Toothache "Twelve Carat Toothache")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Post_Malone_in_Chicago_2020.jpg/250px-Post_Malone_in_Chicago_2020.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Post_Malone_in_Chicago_2020.jpg)

Malone performing in [Rosemont, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemont,_Illinois "Rosemont, Illinois") in February 2020

On March 12, 2020, Malone's concert at [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver")'s [Pepsi Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepsi_Center "Pepsi Center") proceeded as scheduled, drawing a sellout-crowd of 20,000, likely the last large-scale enclosed gathering in the U.S. before [COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-99) Malone received backlash for not cancelling his sold-out arena show amid rising concerns over the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-101) Reportedly, future U.S. tour dates in March were postponed by [Live Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_(events_promoter) "Live Nation (events promoter)") on March 12, 2020.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-102)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-103)

On April 24, 2020, Malone announced that a new album was in progress during a livestream performance.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-105) In late April 2020, Malone performed a livestreamed set consisting entirely of [Nirvana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nirvana_(band) "Nirvana (band)")[covers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") from his home.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Nirvana-106) Malone sang lead vocals and provided rhythm guitar for the set. He was accompanied by drummer [Travis Barker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Barker "Travis Barker"), bassist [Brian Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Lee_(songwriter) "Brian Lee (songwriter)") and lead guitarist Nick Mac. The performance raised over US$5 million for the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization")'s [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") relief fund.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-107) The performance also received praise from Nirvana's surviving members [Krist Novoselic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krist_Novoselic "Krist Novoselic")[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Nirvana-106) and [Dave Grohl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Grohl "Dave Grohl"),[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-108) as well as [Kurt Cobain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Cobain "Kurt Cobain")'s widow [Courtney Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courtney_Love "Courtney Love").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-109)

In June 2020, Malone featured on [Tyla Yaweh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyla_Yaweh "Tyla Yaweh")'s single "[Tommy Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Lee_(song) "Tommy Lee (song)")". The single was followed up with a remix, released July 10, 2020, featuring drums from [Tommy Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Lee "Tommy Lee") himself, as well as a re-recorded guitar instrumental.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-110) A second remix to the song, featuring rapper [Saint Jhn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Jhn "Saint Jhn"), was released subsequently.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-111) On April 30, 2021, Malone was featured on [DJ Khaled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Khaled "DJ Khaled")'s twelfth studio album, _[Khaled Khaled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khaled\_Khaled "Khaled Khaled")_, on the song "[I Did It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Did_It_(DJ_Khaled_song) "I Did It (DJ Khaled song)")" also featuring [DaBaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaBaby "DaBaby"), [Megan Thee Stallion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megan_Thee_Stallion "Megan Thee Stallion"), and [Lil Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Baby "Lil Baby").

On July 9, 2021, Malone released the single "[Motley Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motley_Crew_(song) "Motley Crew (song)")" with an accompanying music video, featuring several guest stars, past collaborators and friends including [Tommy Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Lee "Tommy Lee"), [Tyga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyga "Tyga"), [Tyla Yaweh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyla_Yaweh "Tyla Yaweh") and his manager Dre London. The music video was directed by [Cole Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Bennett "Cole Bennett") of Lyrical Lemonade. On November 5, Malone released "[One Right Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Right_Now "One Right Now")" with [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd"), as the lead single from his upcoming fourth studio album.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-112) On January 26, 2022, during his cover story will _Billboard_, Malone revealed that his fourth studio album would be titled _[Twelve Carat Toothache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve\_Carat\_Toothache "Twelve Carat Toothache")_.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-113) In April 2022, Republic Records relaunched [Mercury Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Records "Mercury Records") with a new roster that includes Post Malone.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-114) On April 27, 2022, Post revealed that _Twelve Carat Toothache_ would be released June 3, 2022.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-115) Malone released the album's second single, "[Cooped Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooped_Up "Cooped Up")" with [Roddy Ricch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roddy_Ricch "Roddy Ricch"), on May 12, 2022.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-116)

On May 14, 2022, he appeared as a musical guest on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_ and performed "Cooped Up" with Ricch, as well as an unreleased song titled "Love/Hate Letter to Alcohol", in which he was joined by [Fleet Foxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Foxes "Fleet Foxes"). Malone had previously confirmed that he had worked with Fleet Foxes frontman [Robin Pecknold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Pecknold "Robin Pecknold") on a song for the album.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-117)

For the 2022 film _[Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chip\_'n\_Dale:\_Rescue\_Rangers\_(film) "Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers (film)")_, Malone covered the theme song from the [1989 television series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chip_'n_Dale:_Rescue_Rangers_(TV_series) "Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers (TV series)"), originally performed by [Jeff Pescetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Pescetto "Jeff Pescetto") in the series and by The Jets in album releases.

On August 12, 2022, the documentary film _Runaway_ premiered on the [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video") channel Freevee. It showed behind the scenes moments from the first leg of the Runaway Tour in 2019, as well as performances from some of the highlighted dates, such as New York City, Chicago, and the 2019 Posty Fest in Arlington.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-118)

### 2023: _The Diamond Collection_ and _Austin_

Main articles: [_The Diamond Collection_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Diamond_Collection "The Diamond Collection") and [_Austin_ (album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_(album) "Austin (album)")

In April 2023, Malone announced that he was working on a new album. On April 14, Malone released "[Chemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_(Post_Malone_song) "Chemical (Post Malone song)")", as the lead single from his upcoming fifth studio album.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-121) On April 21, 2023, Malone released _[The Diamond Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Diamond\_Collection "The Diamond Collection")_, a nine-song compilation of his record-breaking eight [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA "RIAA") Diamond-certified singles, along with the single "Chemical".[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-122) On April 21, 2023, alongside [The Kid Laroi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kid_Laroi "The Kid Laroi"), Malone appeared on "[What You Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_You_Say_(YoungBoy_Never_Broke_Again_song) "What You Say (YoungBoy Never Broke Again song)")", the twenty-fourth cut of [YoungBoy Never Broke Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YoungBoy_Never_Broke_Again "YoungBoy Never Broke Again")'s sixth full-length studio album, _[Don't Try This At Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Try\_This\_at\_Home\_(YoungBoy\_Never\_Broke\_Again\_album) "Don't Try This at Home (YoungBoy Never Broke Again album)")_.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-123)

On May 16, 2023, Malone announced that his fifth studio album, _[Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin\_(album) "Austin (album)")_, would be released on July 28, 2023. On May 19, "[Mourning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourning_(Post_Malone_song) "Mourning (Post Malone song)")" was released as the second single from the album.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-124) On July 14, the third single, "[Overdrive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overdrive_(Post_Malone_song) "Overdrive (Post Malone song)")", was released.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-125) On September 8, the fourth single, "[Enough Is Enough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enough_Is_Enough_(Post_Malone_song) "Enough Is Enough (Post Malone song)")", was released.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-126) On July 17, 2023, Malone collaborated with [Noah Kahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Kahan "Noah Kahan") on a re-released version of Kahan's single "[Dial Drunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dial_Drunk "Dial Drunk")" featuring a new vocal from Malone. The song charted on the [Billboard Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), reaching a peak of number 25.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-127)

### 2024–present: _F-1 Trillion_ and _The Eternal Buzz_

Main articles: [_F-1 Trillion_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-1_Trillion "F-1 Trillion") and [_The Eternal Buzz_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eternal_Buzz "The Eternal Buzz")

On February 11, 2024, Malone performed "[America the Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/America_the_Beautiful "America the Beautiful")" at the [Super Bowl LVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII "Super Bowl LVIII").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:8-128)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:9-129) On February 5, the track list for [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift")'s eleventh studio album, _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tortured\_Poets\_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_, was revealed via her social media accounts, featuring Malone on the first track, "[Fortnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnight_(Taylor_Swift_song) "Fortnight (Taylor Swift song)")". He later posted on his social media supporting this.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-130) The album was released on April 19, 2024, with "Fortnight" being chosen as the lead single and the music video being released later that day. On the day of its release, "Fortnight" set the [single-day streaming record for any song on Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records "List of Spotify streaming records"), surpassing the all-time peak previously held by [Mariah Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey")'s song "[All I Want for Christmas Is You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_I_Want_for_Christmas_Is_You "All I Want for Christmas Is You")" (1994).[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-131)

On March 29, Malone was featured on the track "[Levii's Jeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levii's_Jeans "Levii's Jeans")" off [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé")'s eighth studio album, _[Cowboy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy\_Carter "Cowboy Carter")_.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-132) On May 2, 2024, Malone announced his next single, entitled "[I Had Some Help](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Had_Some_Help "I Had Some Help")" (featuring [Morgan Wallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Wallen "Morgan Wallen")), which released on May 10.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-133) The song earned 167 first-week adds at country radio, making it the second song in history to clear the panel in its first week after [Garth Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garth_Brooks "Garth Brooks") in 1997 with "[Longneck Bottle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longneck_Bottle "Longneck Bottle")".[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Music_Row-134) It also broke [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify")'s single-day country streaming record with nearly 14 million streams, debuted at No. 1 on the streaming platform's Global Daily chart and became its top male collaboration debut of all time, in addition to topping [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music")'s Global chart and [Pandora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandora_(service) "Pandora (service)")'s Top Thumb Hundred chart, upon release.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Music_Row-134) It debuted at No. 18 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_[Country Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Airplay "Country Airplay") chart.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-135)

On June 13, Malone announced the single "[Pour Me a Drink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pour_Me_a_Drink "Pour Me a Drink")" (featuring [Blake Shelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Shelton "Blake Shelton")). It was released on June 21.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-136) On June 18, Malone announced his sixth studio album, _[F-1 Trillion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-1\_Trillion "F-1 Trillion")_, which was released on August 16, 2024.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-137) On July 26, Malone released the third single from the album "[Guy for That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_for_That "Guy for That")" (featuring [Luke Combs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Combs "Luke Combs")).[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-138)

On November 19, Malone announced his eighth concert tour, along with his openers, fellow American rapper, singer, and songwriter [Jelly Roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jelly_Roll_(singer) "Jelly Roll (singer)") and American singer-songwriter and musician [Sierra Ferrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Ferrell "Sierra Ferrell").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-139) On December 25, Malone and Beyoncé gave their first performance of "Levii's Jeans" live as part of Beyoncé's [2024 NFL Halftime Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9_2024_NFL_Halftime_Show "Beyoncé 2024 NFL Halftime Show") set list.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-140) On February 17, 2025, Malone announced the European leg of the tour consisting of various festivals and headline shows, with Jelly Roll also joining as the opening act on select dates.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-141)

For the 50th anniversary celebrations for _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_ on February 14, 2025, Malone reunited with [Nirvana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nirvana_(band) "Nirvana (band)") members to perform "[Smells Like Teen Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smells_Like_Teen_Spirit "Smells Like Teen Spirit")".[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-142)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-143)

On April 13, during the [Coachella 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_2025 "Coachella 2025") festival Malone announced that a new album was in progress.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-144) On April 15, Morgan Wallen announced his next single, "[I Ain't Comin' Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Ain't_Comin'_Back "I Ain't Comin' Back")" with Post Malone, to release on April 18. This was their second collaboration in less than a year, following "[I Had Some Help](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Had_Some_Help "I Had Some Help")".[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-145)

On April 6, 2026, Malone announced his seventh studio album, _[The Eternal Buzz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Eternal\_Buzz "The Eternal Buzz")_, a double album consisting of 40 tracks.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-146) On July 19, the closing ceremony of the [2026 FIFA World Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2026 FIFA World Cup final") it was headlined by Malone. He sang the songs "Chrome Heartbreaker", "Wow" and "Sunflower" with Swae Lee. [[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-147)

## Relationship with the hip-hop community

Malone has been called a "[culture vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_appropriation "Cultural appropriation")" multiple times by different publications and on social media[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-164)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-165) for appropriating [African-American culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_culture "African-American culture").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-166)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-167)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-168) California rapper [Lil B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_B "Lil B") wrote on Twitter in October 2017: "Post Malone is slowly turning into a white dude! Lol he's pushing it, give it a few years he gon be full country and hate blacks lol", with Malone replying in an interview, claiming that his white skin has been "used against him".[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-169) In January 2018, Malone went on an intoxicated rant against people who describe him as a culture vulture.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-170)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-171) In an interview with _GQ_ several days later, Malone said "there's a struggle being a white rapper."[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-172)

In a November 2017 interview with Polish media outlet _Newonce_, Malone said that modern hip-hop music lacks "people talking about real shit" and added that "if you're looking to think about life, don't listen to hip-hop."[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:6-163)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-173) He was criticized for his comments, including by fellow rappers Lil B and [Vince Staples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Staples "Vince Staples").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-174)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-175) Malone later appeared in a video on Twitter, saying that the reason for his comments was that it was a "beer-tasting" interview,[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-176) and going on to say that he loves hip-hop.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-177)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-178)_Newonce_, however, denied that claim, stating that Malone barely drank at all during the interview.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-newonce-179) In the follow-up Malone said, "What I was saying was that when I wanna sit down and cry, I sit down and I listen to [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan") and his guitar. Just like everyone else, no matter how hard you are, no matter where you're from, you're gonna have times where you sit back and reflect on your life and you listen to what you wanna listen to. For me, that's Bob Dylan."[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-newonce-179)

## Other ventures

Since 2018, Malone has released several collaborations with footwear company [Crocs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crocs "Crocs").[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-180)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-181)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-182) The fifth and latest collaboration was released in December 2020.

During his [Runaway Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runaway_Tour_(Post_Malone) "Runaway Tour (Post Malone)") in 2019, he released special-edition [Bud Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Light "Bud Light") beer cans at local stores in 15 cities.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-183) He also released multiple lines of sunglasses in collaboration with Arnette.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-184)

In December 2019, Malone collaborated with [Howlin' Ray's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howlin'_Ray's "Howlin' Ray's") to launch a limited-edition [hot chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_chicken "Hot chicken") sandwich called the "Ghost Malone", which is made with [ghost pepper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_pepper "Ghost pepper")[jack cheese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monterey_Jack_cheese "Monterey Jack cheese") and was exclusively available on [Postmates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postmates "Postmates"). Malone stated that he had been eating at Howlin Ray's since he first came to Los Angeles and "When we first started talking about my own sandwich, I couldn't believe it and the name just came to me right away."[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-185)

In May 2020, he launched his own line of French [rosé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ros%C3%A9 "Rosé") wine, _Maison No. 9_, named after his favourite tarot card, the [Nine of Swords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_of_Swords "Nine of Swords").It sold out in two days upon being made available for sale.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-186) In August 2020, Post Malone invested in [Envy Gaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Envy_Gaming "Envy Gaming"). He became a co-owner of the organization.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-187)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-188)

An enthusiast of the collectible trading card game _[Magic: The Gathering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic:\_The\_Gathering "Magic: The Gathering")_, he collaborated with publisher [Wizards of the Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wizards_of_the_Coast "Wizards of the Coast") in 2022 to create two special supplemental sets: "Secret Lair x Post Malone: Backstage Pass", with cards featuring himself in the title and art, and "Secret Lair x Post Malone: The Lands", with cards featuring his tattoos in the art and flavor texts written by him.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-189) He also owns the unique [One Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Ring "One Ring") card, which he purchased for more than $2 million.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-190)

In April 2023, Malone designed the exterior of a [Raising Cane's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raising_Cane's_Chicken_Fingers "Raising Cane's Chicken Fingers") restaurant location in [Midvale, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midvale,_Utah "Midvale, Utah").[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-191)

In February 2025, Malone and [Mondelez International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mondelez_International "Mondelez International") collaborated to create limited edition [Oreo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oreo "Oreo") cookies featuring salted caramel and shortbread flavored creme, and 9 cookie designs themed after him.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-192)

## Personal life

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Post_Malone_2018.jpg/250px-Post_Malone_2018.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Post_Malone_2018.jpg)

Malone in 2018

As of 2019, Malone resided in [Cottonwood Heights, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cottonwood_Heights,_Utah "Cottonwood Heights, Utah"),[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-193)[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-194) in a multimillion-dollar 12,700-square-foot (1,180 m 2) home.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-195) His former home in Los Angeles' [San Fernando Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Valley "San Fernando Valley") was burglarized on September 1, 2018.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-196)

On August 21, 2018, Malone boarded a plane leaving [Teterboro Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teterboro_Airport "Teterboro Airport") and was scheduled to land at [London Luton Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luton_Airport "Luton Airport"). The tires blew out during takeoff and the plane was rerouted to [Stewart International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stewart_International_Airport "Stewart International Airport") for an emergency landing.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-197) The plane landed safely.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-198) Once the plane had landed, Malone tweeted about the incident, writing "i landed guys. thank you for your prayers. can't believe how many people wished death on me on this website. fuck you. but not today."[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-199)

Malone was involved in a car crash on September 8, 2018. Malone's white [Rolls-Royce Wraith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolls-Royce_Wraith_(2013) "Rolls-Royce Wraith (2013)") was driving through [Santa Monica, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Monica,_California "Santa Monica, California") in the early morning when it collided with another car at 3:30 am. Although no one was severely injured in the incident, several people were treated for minor injuries.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-200)[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-201)

Malone was in a three-year relationship with Ashlen Diaz, ending in November 2018.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Us_Weekly-88) In May 2022, Malone announced that he was expecting his first child with his current girlfriend.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-202) In June, during an appearance on _[The Howard Stern Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Howard\_Stern\_Show "The Howard Stern Show")_, Malone revealed that he and his girlfriend are engaged and had welcomed a daughter. Malone has the initials of his child, "DDP", tattooed on his forehead.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-203)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-204) The song "[Yours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yours_(Post_Malone_song) "Yours (Post Malone song)")" on his album _[F-1 Trillion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-1\_Trillion "F-1 Trillion")_ is inspired by his daughter as he envisions her getting married when she is older.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-205)[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-206)[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-207)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-208) In March 2025, it was revealed that he and his fiancée had quietly split at the end of 2024. His ex-fiancée, later identified as Hee Sung "Jamie" Park, filed documents in Los Angeles in April 2025 asking the court to award her primary physical custody of their daughter. In those documents, Park checked boxes indicating that she is okay with sharing custody (if not awarded full custody) and allowing Malone to have visitations, also known as "parenting time." In the documents, Park also said that their daughter has been living with her since November 2024, and also wants Malone to cover her legal fees.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-209)[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-210) Malone has since been seen in public in the company of a new woman, Christy Lee, a [Parsons School of Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parsons_School_of_Design "Parsons School of Design") student.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-211)[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-212)

### Health

In March 2020, a video surfaced that showed Malone falling and behaving oddly on stage to his song, "[I Fall Apart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Fall_Apart "I Fall Apart")", which made fans worry about his well-being and health.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-213)[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-214) Malone later said that he was "not on drugs and I feel the best I've ever fucking felt in my life". His manager Dre London likewise claimed there was no need to worry and that Malone's behavior was part of the "act". Malone's father Richard said that he does not "want to come across as dismissive to those of you who have expressed concern about Austin. Your sincerity and kindness regarding him is certainly heartwarming and appreciated."[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-215)[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-216)[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-217)

During his 2022 interview with Howard Stern, Malone revealed he has long struggled with alcoholism, but has recovered with the help of his fiancée.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-218)

Post Malone has stated that he has [depersonalization disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depersonalization-derealization_disorder "Depersonalization-derealization disorder") induced by [marijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marijuana "Marijuana") use,[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-m483-219)[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-q212-220) a known possible [side effect of marijuana use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-term_effects_of_cannabis#Depersonalization/derealization_symptoms "Long-term effects of cannabis").[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-x008-221)[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-s208-222)[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-j992-223)

### Political views

Malone has a tattoo of U.S. president [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") on his arm, and has said that Kennedy was "the only President to speak out against the crazy corruption stuff that's going on in our government nowadays."[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-226) In December 2016, Malone stated that if asked to perform at [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s presidential inauguration the following month he would not have been opposed,[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Trump-227) though felt neither Trump nor [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton") were fit for [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") and expressed his support for [Bernie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders "Bernie Sanders") during the election cycle.[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Trump-227)

Malone later expressed a dislike for Trump in a November 2017 interview for _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_. In the same interview, he revealed that he has a large collection of guns and believes it is an American right to own and operate guns. Malone also expressed a strong interest in [conspiracy theories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy_theories "Conspiracy theories") when he said, "There's crazy shit that goes on that we can't explain."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-rollingstone-22) During a trip to Canada in 2018, Malone was interviewed and when asked what the "biggest lie is", he replied "The biggest lie in the world is the U.S. government. It's a fucking reality show and I think there's gonna be a lot of weird shit that happens within our generation that really changes the way of the world."[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-228)

### Religious views

Post Malone grew up in a Christian household in a family of church attendees.[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-p708-229) As of November 2017, he is not religiously affiliated.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-z907-230)

**Austin Richard Post** (born July 4, 1995),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Syr-3) known professionally as **Post Malone**, is an American singer, rapper, songwriter, record producer, and actor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:2-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-5) His music blends various genres including [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"), [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), [trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music "Trap music"), [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"), [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B"), and [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music").

Malone began his musical career in 2010, and earned mainstream recognition with his 2015 [cloud rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_rap "Cloud rap") debut single, "[White Iverson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Iverson "White Iverson")".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-WhiteIversonSC-6) The song led him to sign with [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Schwartz2015-7) and served as lead single for his debut studio album, _[Stoney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoney\_(album) "Stoney (album)")_ (2016), which spawned the [Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification")-certified single "[Congratulations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congratulations_(Post_Malone_song) "Congratulations (Post Malone song)")" (featuring [Quavo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quavo "Quavo")). His second album, _[Beerbongs & Bentleys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beerbongs\_&\_Bentleys "Beerbongs & Bentleys")_ (2018), debuted atop the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and set numerous [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") records. It contained the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number-one singles "[Rockstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockstar_(Post_Malone_song) "Rockstar (Post Malone song)")" (featuring [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage")) and "[Psycho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psycho_(Post_Malone_song) "Psycho (Post Malone song)")" (featuring [Ty Dolla Sign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Dolla_Sign "Ty Dolla Sign")), and was nominated for [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") at the [61st Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "61st Annual Grammy Awards"). His third Hot 100 number-one single, "[Sunflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_(Post_Malone_and_Swae_Lee_song) "Sunflower (Post Malone and Swae Lee song)")", a duet with [Swae Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swae_Lee "Swae Lee"), was released for [the accompanying soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:_Into_the_Spider-Verse_(soundtrack) "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (soundtrack)") to the 2018 animated film _[Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Into\_the\_Spider-Verse "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse")_; it became the highest-certified song in [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") history and was the first to receive a 2× Diamond certification.

Malone's third album, _[Hollywood's Bleeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood's\_Bleeding "Hollywood's Bleeding")_ (2019), became his second project to both debut atop the _Billboard_ 200 and receive Grammy Award nomination for Album of the Year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-8) It spawned the single "[Circles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circles_(Post_Malone_song) "Circles (Post Malone song)")", which spent 61 weeks on the Hot 100, becoming Malone's biggest hit single to date.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-9) Malone's fourth and fifth albums, _[Twelve Carat Toothache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve\_Carat\_Toothache "Twelve Carat Toothache")_ (2022) and [_Austin_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_(album) "Austin (album)") (2023), both peaked at number two on the _Billboard_ 200. In 2024, he topped the _Billboard_ Hot 100 twice more with his guest appearance on [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift")'s "[Fortnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnight_(song) "Fortnight (song)")" and his first [country pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_pop "Country pop") song, "[I Had Some Help](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Had_Some_Help "I Had Some Help")" (featuring [Morgan Wallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Wallen "Morgan Wallen")). The latter served as the lead single for Malone's sixth album and country music debut, _[F-1 Trillion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-1\_Trillion "F-1 Trillion")_ (2024), which became his third number-one album on the _Billboard_ 200.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-10)

Malone is among the [best-selling music artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_music_artists "List of best-selling music artists"), with over 150 million records sold in the US alone according to the RIAA.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-11) His [accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Post_Malone "List of awards and nominations received by Post Malone") include eleven [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award "Billboard Music Award"), five [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"), six [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"), and eighteen [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") nominations.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-13) He holds several _Billboard_ chart records: He is the first solo lead artist to top both the [Rap Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap_Airplay "Rap Airplay") and [Adult Contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_(chart) "Adult Contemporary (chart)") charts, while "Circles" set the record for longest climb to number one (41 weeks) on the [Adult Contemporary chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_(chart) "Adult Contemporary (chart)") by a solo artist.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-14)As of 2025[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Post_Malone&action=edit), Malone is second only to Drake for artists with the most diamond-certified songs, with nine to his name.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-15)

## Early life

Austin Richard Post was born on July 4, 1995,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Syr-3) in [Syracuse, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse,_New_York "Syracuse, New York").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:5-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-17) He was raised by his father, Richard Post, and his stepmother, Jodie. His father had been a [DJ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disc_jockey "Disc jockey") in his youth and introduced Malone to many genres of music including [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"), and [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-Syr-3) When Malone was nine years old,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-18) he and his family moved to [Grapevine, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grapevine,_Texas "Grapevine, Texas"), after his father became the manager of [concessions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concession_stand "Concession stand") for the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") football team.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-papermag-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:0-20) According to Malone, his first foray into professional music began when he played guitar in a local [metalcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metalcore "Metalcore") band.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-AlSharif2019-21) His interest in the genre persisted past this endeavor as he also auditioned as a guitarist for the Texas-based metalcore group [Crown the Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_the_Empire "Crown the Empire") in 2010, but was rejected after his guitar strings broke during the audition. He credited his initial interest in learning guitar to the video game series _[Guitar Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar\_Hero "Guitar Hero")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-rollingstone-22)

Malone has expressed his affinity for [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock") music, and appeared for a DJ set at Emo Nite in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), California, in June 2017, playing songs by [My Chemical Romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Chemical_Romance "My Chemical Romance") at the event.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-23) He says soon afterwards he transitioned to softer rock as well as hip-hop, before beginning to experiment on [FL Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FL_Studio "FL Studio").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-24)

## Career

### 2010–2016: Career beginnings, _August 26th_ and _Stoney_

Main articles: [_August 26th_ (mixtape)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_26th_(mixtape) "August 26th (mixtape)") and [_Stoney_ (album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoney_(album) "Stoney (album)")

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Postmalone-ritual-may7-DREWYORKE-56_%2817275323379%29.jpg/250px-Postmalone-ritual-may7-DREWYORKE-56_%2817275323379%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Postmalone-ritual-may7-DREWYORKE-56_(17275323379).jpg)

Malone performing in 2015

According to Malone, he chose "Post Malone" as his [stage name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stage_name "Stage name") when he was "14 or 15".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-25) The name was rumored to be a reference to the professional basketball player [Karl Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Malone "Karl Malone"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:4-26) but Malone later explained that "Post" is his last name, and he used a "rap name generator" to get "Malone".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-vh1.com-27)

In 2010, Malone reportedly played guitar in the [metalcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metalcore "Metalcore") band Ashley's Arrival (also known as Saving Summer) during his high school years. That same year, he auditioned for [Crown the Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_the_Empire "Crown the Empire") as a guitarist. In a 2016 interview, vocalist Andy Leo recalled that Malone broke a guitar string during the audition and was not selected.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-28)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-AsA-1)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-29)

In late 2011, Malone released his oldest known solo project, an 11-track [mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixtape "Mixtape") titled _Manifest Destiny_.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-30)

In 2013, Malone was a member of the band Love In Colors, in which he performed as a vocalist and guitarist.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-LoveInColors-2)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-31)

At age 17, Malone, along with his friend Jazzy Eff, released a parody [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop")[ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") song called "Why Don't You Love Me" under the alias Leon DeChino, intended for a school project. The song reappeared online in 2016. Malone later referred to the DeChino alias on his song "[Psycho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psycho_(Post_Malone_song) "Psycho (Post Malone song)")".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-33)

At the age of 18, using audio editor [Audacity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audacity_(audio_editor) "Audacity (audio editor)"), Malone released his second mixtape, _Y.A.T.R._, also known as _Youngin' After Them Riches_, in 2014.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-35) He showed it to some of his classmates at [Grapevine High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grapevine_High_School "Grapevine High School").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-rollingstone-22)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:2-4) He was voted "Most Likely to Become Famous" by his classmates as a senior in high school. He worked at a [Chicken Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken_Express "Chicken Express") as a teenager.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-rollingstone-22)

Malone later enrolled in [Tarrant County College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarrant_County_College "Tarrant County College"), but dropped out.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-36) After leaving college, Malone moved to Los Angeles with his longtime friend Jason Probst, a professional game streamer.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-39)

After moving to Los Angeles, Malone, Probst, and several other producers and artists formed the music group BLCKVRD and recorded music together.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-40) Several members of the group, including Malone, moved into a house in the [San Fernando Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Valley "San Fernando Valley") together. While living in the San Fernando Valley, Malone met record producers [FKi 1st](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FKi_1st "FKi 1st") and Sauce Lord Rich, who formed the production team [FKi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FKi_(production_team) "FKi (production team)"), as well as Rex Kudo, who produced several of Malone's tracks, including "[White Iverson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Iverson "White Iverson")".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:5-16) Malone recorded the song two days after writing it.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:2-4) The lyrics of "White Iverson" allude to [Basketball Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naismith_Memorial_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame") player [Allen Iverson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Iverson "Allen Iverson").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:1-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:3-42)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-:4-26) In February 2015, upon completion, it was uploaded to Malone's SoundCloud account.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-WhiteIversonSC-6) On July 19, 2015, Malone released a [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "White Iverson". The single received praise from rappers [Mac Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Miller "Mac Miller") and [Wiz Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiz_Khalifa "Wiz Khalifa").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-rollingstone-22)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-success-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-44) However the song was mocked by [Earl Sweatshirt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Sweatshirt "Earl Sweatshirt").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone#cite_note-47)
