Musical artist

**John Robert** "**Joe**" **Cocker** (20 May 1944 – 22 December 2014) was an English singer known for his gritty, bluesy voice and dynamic stage performances that featured expressive body movements. Most of his best known singles were interpretations of songs written by others, such as "[Feelin' Alright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feelin'_Alright%3F#Joe_Cocker_version "Feelin' Alright?")" and "[Unchain My Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unchain_My_Heart_(song)#Notable_cover_versions "Unchain My Heart (song)")", though Cocker composed original songs for most of his albums as well, often in conjunction with songwriting partner [Chris Stainton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Stainton "Chris Stainton").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-Indep23dec14-1)

His [debut album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/With_a_Little_Help_from_My_Friends_(Joe_Cocker_album) "With a Little Help from My Friends (Joe Cocker album)") featured a recording of [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles")' "[With a Little Help from My Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/With_a_Little_Help_from_My_Friends#Joe_Cocker_version "With a Little Help from My Friends")", which was featured as its title track and brought him to near-instant stardom. The song reached number one in the UK in 1968, became a staple of his many live shows ([Woodstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock "Woodstock") and the [Isle of Wight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_of_Wight_Festival_1969 "Isle of Wight Festival 1969") in 1969, the [Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_at_the_Palace "Party at the Palace") in 2002) and was also known as the theme song for the late 1980s American TV series _[The Wonder Years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wonder\_Years "The Wonder Years")_. He continued his success with his [second album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker! "Joe Cocker!"), which included a second Beatles song, "[She Came In Through the Bathroom Window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She_Came_In_Through_the_Bathroom_Window#Notable_cover_versions "She Came In Through the Bathroom Window")". A hastily thrown-together 1970 US tour led to the live double-album _[Mad Dogs & Englishmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Dogs\_&\_Englishmen\_(album) "Mad Dogs & Englishmen (album)")_, which featured an all-star band organised by [Leon Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Russell "Leon Russell"). His 1974 recording of "[You Are So Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Are_So_Beautiful "You Are So Beautiful")" reached number five in the US, and became his [signature song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature_song "Signature song"). Cocker's best-selling song was the US number one "[Up Where We Belong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up_Where_We_Belong "Up Where We Belong")", a duet with American singer-songwriter [Jennifer Warnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Warnes "Jennifer Warnes") that earned a 1983 [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"). He released a total of 22 studio albums over a 43-year recording career.

In 1993, Cocker was nominated for the [Brit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award "Brit Award") for Best British Male Solo Artist. He was awarded a bronze [Sheffield Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield_Legends "Sheffield Legends") plaque in his hometown in 2007, and received an [OBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OBE "OBE") the following year for services to music.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-Brits-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-OBE-3) Cocker was ranked number 97 on _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_'s 100 greatest singers list.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-4) Cocker was posthumously inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") in November 2025.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-rr25-6)

## Early life (1944–1960)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Cocker&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life (1944–1960)")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Sheffield_Legends_Joe_Cocker.jpg/250px-Sheffield_Legends_Joe_Cocker.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sheffield_Legends_Joe_Cocker.jpg)

[Sheffield Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield_Legends "Sheffield Legends") plaque in Cocker's home city of [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"), England

Cocker was born on 20 May 1944 at 38 Tasker Road, [Crookes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crookes "Crookes"), [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"). He was the youngest son of a civil servant, Harold Norman Cocker (1907–2001), at the time of his son's birth serving as an [aircraftman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraftman "Aircraftman") in the [Royal Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force"), and Madge (née Lee).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-7) According to differing family stories, Cocker received his nickname of Joe either from playing a childhood game called "Cowboy Joe", or from a local window cleaner named Joe.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-8)

Cocker's main musical influences growing up were [Ray Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Charles "Ray Charles") and [Lonnie Donegan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lonnie_Donegan "Lonnie Donegan"). Cocker's first experience singing in public was at age 12 when his elder brother Victor invited him on stage to sing during a gig of his [skiffle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skiffle "Skiffle") group. In 1960, along with three friends, Cocker formed his first group, the Cavaliers. For the group's first performance at a youth club, they were required to pay the price of admission before entering. The Cavaliers eventually broke up after a year and Cocker left school to become an apprentice [gasfitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasfitter "Gasfitter") working for the [East Midlands Gas Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Midlands_Gas_Board "East Midlands Gas Board"), later [British Gas Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Gas_Corporation "British Gas Corporation"), while simultaneously pursuing a career in music.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean20036%E2%80%939-9)

Cocker is not related to fellow Sheffield-born musician [Jarvis Cocker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarvis_Cocker "Jarvis Cocker"), despite a rumour circulated by Jarvis's father, Australian radio presenter [Mac Cocker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Cocker "Mac Cocker"), who allowed listeners to believe that he was Joe's brother.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-11) However, Joe was a friend of the family and even did some babysitting for Jarvis when the latter was an infant.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-clashmusic-12)

## Career (1961–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Cocker&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career (1961–2014)")]

### Early career and the Grease Band (1961–1969)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Cocker&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career and the Grease Band (1961–1969)")]

In 1961, under the stage name "Vance Arnold", Cocker started a new group, Vance Arnold and the Avengers.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-Story-13) The name was a combination of Vince Everett ([Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley")'s character in _[Jailhouse Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jailhouse\_Rock\_(film) "Jailhouse Rock (film)")_, which Cocker misheard as Vance) and country singer [Eddy Arnold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddy_Arnold "Eddy Arnold").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200316-14) The group mostly played in the [pubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pub "Pub") of Sheffield,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-Story-13) performing [Chuck Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Berry "Chuck Berry") and [Ray Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Charles "Ray Charles") songs. Cocker developed an interest in [blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues "Blues") music and sought out recordings by [John Lee Hooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lee_Hooker "John Lee Hooker"), [Muddy Waters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muddy_Waters "Muddy Waters"), [Lightnin' Hopkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightnin'_Hopkins "Lightnin' Hopkins") and [Howlin' Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howlin'_Wolf "Howlin' Wolf").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-Hale-15) In 1963, they booked their first significant gig when they supported [the Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones") at [Sheffield City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield_City_Hall "Sheffield City Hall").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-16)

In 1964, Cocker signed a recording contract as a solo act with [Decca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decca_Records "Decca Records") and released his debut single, a recording of [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles")' "[I'll Cry Instead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'll_Cry_Instead "I'll Cry Instead")" (with [Big Jim Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Jim_Sullivan "Big Jim Sullivan") and [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page") playing guitars). Despite extensive promotion from Decca lauding his youth and working-class roots, the record was a flop and his recording contract with Decca lapsed at the end of 1964.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200328-17) After Cocker recorded the single, he dropped his stage name and formed a new group, Joe Cocker's Blues Band. There is only one known recording of Joe Cocker's Blues Band on an EP given out by [The Sheffield College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sheffield_College "The Sheffield College") during Rag Week and called _Rag Goes Mad at the Mojo_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-18)

In 1966, after a year-long hiatus from music, Cocker teamed up with [Chris Stainton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Stainton "Chris Stainton"), whom he had met several years before, to form [the Grease Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Grease_Band "The Grease Band").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-Story-13) The Grease Band was named after Cocker read an interview with jazz keyboardist [Jimmy Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Smith_(musician) "Jimmy Smith (musician)"), where Smith positively described another musician as "having a lot of grease". Like the Avengers, Cocker's group mostly played in pubs in and around Sheffield. The Grease Band came to the attention of [Denny Cordell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denny_Cordell "Denny Cordell"), the producer of [Procol Harum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Procol_Harum "Procol Harum"), [the Moody Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Moody_Blues "The Moody Blues") and [Georgie Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgie_Fame "Georgie Fame"). Cocker recorded the single "Marjorine" without the Grease Band for Cordell in a London studio. He then moved to London with Chris Stainton, and the Grease Band was dissolved. Cordell set Cocker up with a residency at the [Marquee Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquee_Club "Marquee Club") in London, and a "new" Grease Band was formed with Stainton and keyboardist [Tommy Eyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Eyre "Tommy Eyre").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200343%E2%80%9345-19)

In 1968, Cocker found commercial success with a rearrangement of "[With a Little Help from My Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/With_a_Little_Help_from_My_Friends#Joe_Cocker_version "With a Little Help from My Friends")", another Beatles song. The recording features lead guitar from [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page"), drumming by [B. J. Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Wilson "B. J. Wilson"), backing vocals from [Sue and Sunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sue_and_Sunny "Sue and Sunny"), and Tommy Eyre on organ. The single remained in the top ten of the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") for thirteen weeks before eventually reaching number one, on 9 November 1968.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200348%E2%80%9349-20) It also reached number 68 on the US charts.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200354-21)

The new touring line-up of Cocker's Grease Band featured [Henry McCullough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_McCullough "Henry McCullough") on lead guitar, who would go on to briefly play with McCartney's [Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wings_(band) "Wings (band)"). After touring the UK with [the Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who") in autumn 1968[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-22) and [Gene Pitney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Pitney "Gene Pitney") and [Marmalade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marmalade_(band) "Marmalade (band)") in early winter 1969, the Grease Band embarked on their first tour of the US in spring 1969. Cocker's album _[With a Little Help from My Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/With\_a\_Little\_Help\_from\_My\_Friends\_(Joe\_Cocker\_album) "With a Little Help from My Friends (Joe Cocker album)")_ was released soon after their arrival and made number 35 on the American charts, eventually going gold.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200354%E2%80%9355-23)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Woodstock_redmond_cocker01.jpg/250px-Woodstock_redmond_cocker01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Woodstock_redmond_cocker01.jpg)

Cocker performing at [Woodstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock "Woodstock") in 1969

During his US tour, Cocker played at several large festivals, including the [Newport Pop Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport_Pop_Festival "Newport Pop Festival") and the [Denver Pop Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Pop_Festival "Denver Pop Festival"). In August, Denny Cordell heard about the planned concert in [Woodstock, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock,_New_York "Woodstock, New York") and convinced organiser [Artie Kornfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artie_Kornfeld "Artie Kornfeld") to book Cocker and the Grease Band for the [Woodstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock "Woodstock") Festival. The group had to be flown into the festival by helicopter due to the large crowds. They performed several songs, including "[Feelin' Alright?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feelin'_Alright%3F#Joe_Cocker_version "Feelin' Alright?")", "Something's Comin' On", "[Let's Go Get Stoned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let's_Go_Get_Stoned#Other_notable_covers "Let's Go Get Stoned")", "[I Shall Be Released](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Shall_Be_Released#Notable_covers "I Shall Be Released")" and "With a Little Help from My Friends". Cocker would later say that the experience was "like an eclipse... it was a very special day."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200358%E2%80%9360-24)

Directly after Woodstock, Cocker released his second album, _[Joe Cocker!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe\_Cocker! "Joe Cocker!")_ Impressed by his version of "With a Little Help from My Friends", [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney") and [George Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Harrison "George Harrison") allowed Cocker to use their songs "[She Came In Through the Bathroom Window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She_Came_In_Through_the_Bathroom_Window#Notable_cover_versions "She Came In Through the Bathroom Window")" and "[Something](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Something_(Beatles_song)#Joe_Cocker_demo "Something (Beatles song)")" for the album.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200361-25) Recorded during a break in touring in the spring and summer, the album reached number 11 on the US charts and garnered a second UK [hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chart_hit "Chart hit") with the [Leon Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Russell "Leon Russell") song, "[Delta Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Lady "Delta Lady")".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In August 1969, Cocker performed at the [Isle of Wight Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_of_Wight_Festival_1969 "Isle of Wight Festival 1969") at [Wootton Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wootton_Bridge "Wootton Bridge"), Isle of Wight, England.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-26) Throughout 1969 he was featured on variety TV shows like _[The Ed Sullivan Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ed\_Sullivan\_Show "The Ed Sullivan Show")_ and _[This Is Tom Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Is\_Tom\_Jones "This Is Tom Jones")_. Onstage, he exhibited an idiosyncratic physical intensity, flailing his arms and playing [air guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_guitar "Air guitar"). At the end of the year Cocker was unwilling to embark on another US tour, so he dissolved the Grease Band.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Mad Dogs & Englishmen (1970–1971)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Cocker&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mad Dogs & Englishmen (1970–1971)")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/Joe_Cocker_72.jpg/250px-Joe_Cocker_72.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Cocker_72.jpg)

Cocker in concert at Palasport, Rome, July 1972

Despite Cocker's reluctance to venture out on the road again, an American tour had already been booked so he had to quickly form a new band to fulfill his contractual obligations. It proved to be a large group of more than 20 musicians, including pianist and bandleader [Leon Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Russell "Leon Russell"), three drummers – [Jim Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Gordon_(musician) "Jim Gordon (musician)"), [Jim Keltner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Keltner "Jim Keltner"), and Chuck Blackwell, and backing vocalists [Rita Coolidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Coolidge "Rita Coolidge") and [Claudia Lennear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudia_Lennear "Claudia Lennear"). Denny Cordell christened the new band "Mad Dogs & Englishmen", after the [Noël Coward song of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Dogs_and_Englishmen_(song) "Mad Dogs and Englishmen (song)") (with its refrain, "Mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun"). Cocker's music evolved into a more bluesy type of rock, comparable to that of [the Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-27)

During the ensuing Mad Dogs & Englishmen tour (later described by drummer Jim Keltner as "a big, wild party"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200370-28) Cocker toured 48 cities, recorded a live album, and received positive reviews from _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ and _[Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life\_(magazine) "Life (magazine)")_ for his performances. However, the pace of the tour was exhausting. Russell and Cocker had personal problems; Cocker became depressed and began drinking excessively as the tour wound down in May 1970. Meanwhile, he enjoyed several chart entries in the United States with cover versions of "[Feelin' Alright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feelin'_Alright%3F#Joe_Cocker_version "Feelin' Alright?")" (originally recorded by [Traffic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_(band) "Traffic (band)")) and "[Cry Me a River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cry_Me_a_River_(Arthur_Hamilton_song)#Notable_recordings "Cry Me a River (Arthur Hamilton song)")".[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

His version of [the Box Tops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Box_Tops "The Box Tops")' hit "[The Letter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Letter_(Box_Tops_song)#Joe_Cocker_renditions "The Letter (Box Tops song)")", which appeared on the live album and film, _[Mad Dogs & Englishmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Dogs\_&\_Englishmen\_(album) "Mad Dogs & Englishmen (album)")_, became his first US Top Ten [hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_record "Hit record"). After spending several months in Los Angeles, Cocker returned home to Sheffield, where his family became increasingly concerned with his deteriorating physical and [mental health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_health "Mental health"). In the summer of 1971, [A&M Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A&M_Records "A&M Records") released the single "High Time We Went". This became a hit, reaching number 22 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart, but was not issued on an album until November 1972 on Cocker's [self-titled album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker_(album) "Joe Cocker (album)").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### On the road (1972–1979)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Cocker&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: On the road (1972–1979)")]

In early 1972, after nearly two years away from music, Cocker went on tour with a group that Chris Stainton had formed. He opened with a performance in [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden") which was attended by about 20,000 people. After touring the United States, he embarked on a European tour where he played to large audiences in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan") and Germany. He then returned to the United States for another tour in autumn 1972. During these tours the group cut the songs that would be part of his newest album, a [self-titled release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker_(album) "Joe Cocker (album)"). A mixture of live songs and studio recordings, the album peaked at number 30 on the US charts.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200396-29)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Joe_cocker.jpg/250px-Joe_cocker.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_cocker.jpg)

Cocker performing on 16 October 1980 at the [National Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Stadium_(Ireland) "National Stadium (Ireland)"), Dublin

In October 1972, when Cocker toured Australia, he and six members of his entourage were arrested in [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide") for possession of [marijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marijuana "Marijuana").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-30) The next day, in [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne"), assault charges were laid after a brawl at the Commodore Chateau Hotel,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-31) and the [Australian Federal Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Federal_Police "Australian Federal Police") gave Cocker 48 hours to leave the country. This caused huge public outcry in Australia, as Cocker was a high-profile overseas artist and had a strong support base, especially among the [baby boomers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_boomers "Baby boomers") who were coming of age and able to vote for the first time. It sparked hefty debate about the use and legalisation of marijuana in Australia, and gained Cocker the nickname "the Mad Dog".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003101-32)

Shortly after the Australian tour, Stainton retired from his music career to establish his own recording studio. After his friend's departure and his estrangement from his longtime producer Denny Cordell, Cocker sank into depression and began using heroin. In June 1973, he kicked the habit but continued to drink heavily.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003110-33)

At the end of 1973, Cocker returned to the studio to record a new album, _[I Can Stand a Little Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Can\_Stand\_a\_Little\_Rain "I Can Stand a Little Rain")_. The album, released in August 1974, was number 11 on the US charts and one single, a recording of [Billy Preston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Preston "Billy Preston")'s "[You Are So Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Are_So_Beautiful "You Are So Beautiful")", reached the number 5 slot.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003112%E2%80%9314-34) Despite positive reviews for the album, Cocker struggled with live performances, largely due to his problems with alcohol. One such instance was reported in a 1974 issue of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_, which said that during two [West Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast_of_the_United_States "West Coast of the United States") performances in October of that year he threw up onstage.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-35)

In January 1975, he released a second album that had been recorded at the same time as _I Can Stand a Little Rain_, _[Jamaica Say You Will](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica\_Say\_You\_Will "Jamaica Say You Will")_. To promote his new album, Cocker embarked on another tour of Australia, made possible by the country's new [Labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Labor_Party "Australian Labor Party") government. In late 1975, he contributed vocals on a number of the tracks on [Bo Diddley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Diddley "Bo Diddley")'s _The 20th Anniversary of Rock 'n' Roll_ all-star album. He also recorded a new album in a [Kingston, Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston,_Jamaica "Kingston, Jamaica") studio, _[Stingray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stingray\_(album) "Stingray (album)")_. However, record sales were disappointing; the album reached only number 70 on the US charts.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003122-36)

In May 1976, Cocker headlined an 11-date tour of Canada, and on 2 October, Cocker performed "Feelin' Alright" on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live "Saturday Night Live")_. [John Belushi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Belushi "John Belushi") joined him onstage doing his famous impersonation of Cocker's stage movements. At the time, Cocker was $800,000 in debt to [A&M Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A&M_Records "A&M Records") and struggling with alcoholism. Several months later, he met producer [Michael Lang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Lang_(producer) "Michael Lang (producer)"), who agreed to manage him on the condition that he stay sober. With a new band, Cocker embarked on a tour of New Zealand, Australia and South America. He then recorded a new album with [session](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Session_musician "Session musician") work by [Steve Gadd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Gadd "Steve Gadd") and [Chuck Rainey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Rainey "Chuck Rainey"). In the autumn of 1978, Cocker toured North America promoting his album, _[Luxury You Can Afford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxury\_You\_Can\_Afford "Luxury You Can Afford")_. Despite this effort, it received mixed reviews, selling around 300,000 copies.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003140-37)

In 1979, Cocker joined the "Woodstock in Europe" tour, which featured musicians like [Arlo Guthrie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlo_Guthrie "Arlo Guthrie") and [Richie Havens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Havens "Richie Havens") who had played at the 1969 Woodstock Festival. He also performed in New York's [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park") to an audience of 20,000 people. The concert was recorded and released as the live album, _Live in New York_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003143-38)

### 1980s (1980–1989)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Cocker&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1980s (1980–1989)")]

In 1982, Cocker recorded two songs with the jazz group [the Crusaders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Crusaders_(Houston_group) "The Crusaders (Houston group)") on their album _[Standing Tall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing\_Tall\_(The\_Crusaders\_album) "Standing Tall (The Crusaders album)")_. One song, "I'm So Glad I'm Standing Here Today", was nominated for a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") and Cocker performed it with the Crusaders at the awards ceremony. The Crusaders wrote this song with Cocker in mind to sing it. Cocker then released a new reggae-influenced album, _[Sheffield Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield\_Steel "Sheffield Steel")_, recorded with the [Compass Point All Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compass_Point_All_Stars "Compass Point All Stars"), produced by [Chris Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Blackwell "Chris Blackwell") and [Alex Sadkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Sadkin "Alex Sadkin").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Also in 1982, Cocker recorded the duet "[Up Where We Belong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up_Where_We_Belong "Up Where We Belong")" with the American singer [Jennifer Warnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Warnes "Jennifer Warnes") for the soundtrack of the film _[An Officer and a Gentleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_Officer\_and\_a\_Gentleman "An Officer and a Gentleman")_. The song was an international hit, reaching number 1 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), and winning a [Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Performance_by_a_Duo_or_Group_with_Vocals "Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals"). The duet also won an [Academy Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song"), and Cocker and Warnes performed the song at the awards ceremony.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-39) Several days later, he was invited to perform "[You Are So Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Are_So_Beautiful "You Are So Beautiful")" with [Ray Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Charles "Ray Charles") in a television tribute to the musician. In 1983, Cocker joined a star-studded line-up of British musicians, including [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page"), [Eric Clapton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Clapton "Eric Clapton"), [Jeff Beck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Beck "Jeff Beck"), [Steve Winwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Winwood "Steve Winwood") and [Bill Wyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Wyman "Bill Wyman") for singer [Ronnie Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_Lane "Ronnie Lane")'s [1983 tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARMS_Charity_Concerts "ARMS Charity Concerts") to raise money for the London-based organisation [Action for Research into Multiple Sclerosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_for_Research_into_Multiple_Sclerosis "Action for Research into Multiple Sclerosis"), in particular because Lane was beginning to suffer from the degenerative disease.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-40)

While on another tour that year, Cocker was arrested by Austrian police after refusing to perform because of inadequate sound equipment. The charges were eventually dropped and Cocker was released.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003160-41) Shortly after the incident, he released his ninth studio album, _[Civilized Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilized\_Man "Civilized Man")_. His next album _[Cocker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocker\_(album) "Cocker (album)")_ was dedicated to his mother, Madge, who died when he was recording in the studio with producer [Terry Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Manning "Terry Manning"). A track from the album, a cover of [Randy Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Newman "Randy Newman")'s "[You Can Leave Your Hat On](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Can_Leave_Your_Hat_On#Joe_Cocker_version "You Can Leave Your Hat On")", was featured in the 1986 film _[9½ Weeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9%C2%BD\_Weeks "9½ Weeks")_. The album eventually went Platinum on the European charts.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003167-42) His song "Love Lives On" was featured in the 1987 film _[Harry and the Hendersons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_and\_the\_Hendersons "Harry and the Hendersons")_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-43) His 1987 album _[Unchain My Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unchain\_My\_Heart\_(album) "Unchain My Heart (album)")_ was nominated for a Grammy Award, although it did not win. _[One Night of Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Night\_of\_Sin "One Night of Sin")_ was also a commercial success, surpassing _Unchain My Heart_ in sales and yielding his final Top 20 hit in the United States, "When The Night Comes", written by [Bryan Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Adams "Bryan Adams"), [Jim Vallance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Vallance "Jim Vallance") and [Diane Warren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Warren "Diane Warren") that peaked at number 11 in January 1990.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1984, Cocker released the song "Edge of a Dream", which was included on the soundtrack of the film _[Teachers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teachers\_(film) "Teachers (film)")_. In Brazil, the song became popular as part of the soundtrack of the soap opera [Corpo a Corpo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpo_a_Corpo "Corpo a Corpo"), broadcast on [Rede Globo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rede_Globo "Rede Globo") in 1985.

Throughout the 1980s, Cocker continued to tour around the world, playing to large audiences in Europe, Australia and the United States. In 1986, he met the Italian singer [Zucchero Fornaciari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zucchero_Fornaciari "Zucchero Fornaciari"), who dedicated a song (_Nuovo, meraviglioso amico_, in _Rispetto_) to the English bluesman. After that Cocker took part in some concerts of the promotional tours for the albums _[Blue's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue's "Blue's")_ (1987) and _[Oro Incenso & Birra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oro\_Incenso\_&\_Birra "Oro Incenso & Birra")_ (1989). In 1988, he performed at London's [Royal Albert Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Albert_Hall "Royal Albert Hall") and appeared on _[The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Johnny\_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson")_.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003178-44) After [Barclay James Harvest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclay_James_Harvest "Barclay James Harvest") and [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan"), Cocker was the first to give rock concerts in the [German Democratic Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Democratic_Republic "German Democratic Republic"), in [East Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Berlin "East Berlin") and [Dresden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dresden "Dresden"). The venue, the _Blüherwiese_, next to the [Rudolf–Harbig–Stadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gl%C3%BCcksgas_Stadium "Glücksgas Stadium"), bears the vernacular name _Cockerwiese_ ('Cocker meadow') today.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-45) He also performed for US President [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") at an inauguration concert in 1989.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-46)

### Later career (1990–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Cocker&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Later career (1990–2014)")]

In 1992, Cocker's version of [Bryan Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Adams "Bryan Adams")' "Feels Like Forever" made the [UK Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Top_40 "UK Top 40").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003189-47) Also in 1992, Cocker teamed with Canadian rocker [Sass Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sass_Jordan "Sass Jordan") to sing "Trust in Me", which was featured on _[The Bodyguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bodyguard\_(soundtrack) "The Bodyguard (soundtrack)")_ soundtrack. At the 1993 [Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards "Brit Awards"), Cocker was nominated for British Male Solo Artist.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-Brits-2) Cocker performed the Saturday opening set at [Woodstock '94](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock_'94 "Woodstock '94") as one of the few alumni who played at the original Woodstock Festival in 1969 and was well received.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-48)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/JoeCocker03.jpg/250px-JoeCocker03.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JoeCocker03.jpg)

Cocker playing [air guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_guitar "Air guitar") in [Hallandale Beach, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallandale_Beach,_Florida "Hallandale Beach, Florida"), in 2003

On 3 June 2002, Cocker performed "With A Little Help From My Friends" accompanied by [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins") on drums and [Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_(band) "Queen (band)") guitarist [Brian May](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_May "Brian May") at the [Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_at_the_Palace "Party at the Palace") concert in the grounds of [Buckingham Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckingham_Palace "Buckingham Palace"), an event in commemoration of the [Golden Jubilee of Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Golden Jubilee of Elizabeth II").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-49) In 2007, Cocker appeared playing minor characters in the film _[Across the Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Across\_the\_Universe\_(film) "Across the Universe (film)")_, as the lead singer on another Beatles' hit, "[Come Together](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Together "Come Together")".[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-50) Cocker was awarded an [OBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OBE "OBE") in the Queen's 2007 Birthday Honours list for services to music.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-OBE-3) To celebrate receiving his award in mid December 2007, Cocker played two concerts in London and in his home town of Sheffield where he was awarded a bronze [Sheffield Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield_Legends "Sheffield Legends") plaque outside [Sheffield Town Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield_Town_Hall "Sheffield Town Hall").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-51)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/Joe_Cocker_Sochi.JPG/250px-Joe_Cocker_Sochi.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Cocker_Sochi.JPG)

Cocker performing in 2011

In April and May 2009, Cocker conducted a North American tour in support of his album _[Hymn for My Soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymn\_for\_My\_Soul "Hymn for My Soul")_. He sang the vocals on "[Little Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Wing "Little Wing")" for the [Carlos Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Santana "Carlos Santana") album, _[Guitar Heaven: The Greatest Guitar Classics of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar\_Heaven:\_The\_Greatest\_Guitar\_Classics\_of\_All\_Time "Guitar Heaven: The Greatest Guitar Classics of All Time")_, released on 21 September 2010. In the autumn of 2010, Cocker toured Europe promoting his studio album _Hard Knocks_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2000, Cocker was the opening act in select cities in the United States and Europe for [Tina Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tina_Turner "Tina Turner")'s [Twenty Four Seven Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty_Four_Seven_Tour "Twenty Four Seven Tour"). He returned to Australia in 2008 and again in 2011, the latter of which featured [George Thorogood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Thorogood "George Thorogood") and the Destroyers as an opening act.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-52)

On 20 March 2011, Cocker took part in a benefit concert for [Cornell Dupree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_Dupree "Cornell Dupree") at [B.B. King's Blues Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.B._King's_Blues_Club "B.B. King's Blues Club") in New York City. Dupree played on four Cocker albums: _I Can Stand A Little Rain_ (1974), _Jamaica Say You Will_ (1975), _Stingray_ (1976) and _Luxury You Can Afford_ (1978). Dupree's band Stuff was also Cocker's backing band on a tour promoting _Stingray_ in 1976.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Cocker kept recording and touring throughout his later years. 2012's _[Fire it up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire\_It\_Up\_(Joe\_Cocker\_album) "Fire It Up (Joe Cocker album)")_, which would turn out to be Cocker's last studio album, was followed by an extensive tour, consisting of a US leg in 2012 and a European run in 2013. He played 25 shows in Germany alone on the European leg of the tour, which reflects the popularity Cocker enjoyed there.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-53) The full show of 22 April at [Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne "Cologne")'s [Lanxess Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lanxess_Arena "Lanxess Arena") was recorded and released on CD and DVD under the title _Fire it up Live_ later in 2013. The last concert on the tour, which was to be Cocker's final live performance, was at the [Loreley Open Air Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freilichtb%C3%BChne_Loreley "Freilichtbühne Loreley") in [Sankt Goarshausen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sankt_Goarshausen "Sankt Goarshausen") on 7 September 2013.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Tributes and acclaim

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Cocker&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Tributes and acclaim")]

In 1994, fellow Yorkshire musician [Philip Oakey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Oakey "Philip Oakey"), on behalf of his group, [the Human League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Human_League "The Human League"), said that Cocker was their "hero".[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-54)

The two remaining living ex-Beatles, [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney") and [Ringo Starr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ringo_Starr "Ringo Starr"), were among those who paid tribute to the singer following his death, while Cocker's agent, Barrie Marshall, said that Cocker was "without doubt the greatest rock/soul singer ever to come out of Britain".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-McCartney-55) McCartney commented:

> He was a lovely northern lad who I loved a lot and, like many people, I loved his singing. I was especially pleased when he decided to cover 'With a Little Help from My Friends' and I remember him and (producer) Denny Cordell coming round to the studio in [Savile Row](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savile_Row "Savile Row") (central London) and playing me what they'd recorded and it was just mind-blowing, totally turned the song into a soul anthem and I was forever grateful to him for doing that.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-McCartney-55)

On 11 September 2015, a "Mad Dogs & Englishmen" tribute concert to Joe Cocker was performed at the Lockn' Festival featuring [Tedeschi Trucks Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tedeschi_Trucks_Band "Tedeschi Trucks Band"), [Chris Stainton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Stainton "Chris Stainton"), [Leon Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Russell "Leon Russell"), [Rita Coolidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Coolidge "Rita Coolidge"), [Claudia Lennear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudia_Lennear "Claudia Lennear"), [Pamela Polland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Polland "Pamela Polland"), [Doyle Bramhall II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doyle_Bramhall_II "Doyle Bramhall II"), [Dave Mason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Mason "Dave Mason"), [John Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bell_(musician) "John Bell (musician)"), [Warren Haynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Haynes "Warren Haynes") and [Chris Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Robinson_(singer) "Chris Robinson (singer)"), among others. In commemoration,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-56) a Joe Cocker Mad Dogs and Englishmen Memory Book was created by [Linda Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Wolf "Linda Wolf") to celebrate the event.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-57) In late 2021, the feature-length documentary _[Learning to Live Together](https://learningtolivetogether.com/)_ was released documenting the reunion concert.

In 2017, a feature-length documentary film about Cocker titled _Joe Cocker: Mad Dog with Soul_ was released.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-58)

## Personal life and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Cocker&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Personal life and death")]

In 1963, Cocker began dating Eileen Webster, also a resident of Sheffield. The couple dated intermittently for the next 13 years.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean200315-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-62)

In 1978, Cocker moved onto a ranch owned by [Jane Fonda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Fonda "Jane Fonda") in [Santa Barbara, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Barbara,_California "Santa Barbara, California"). Pam Baker, a local summer camp director and fan of Cocker's music, had persuaded the actress to lend the house to Cocker. Baker began dating Cocker, and they married on 11 October 1987.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBean2003171-63)

While performing a concert at [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden") on 17 September 2014, fellow pop musician [Billy Joel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Joel "Billy Joel") stated that Cocker was "not very well right now" and endorsed Cocker for induction into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") before his tribute performance of "With a Little Help from My Friends".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-64)

Cocker died from [lung cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung_cancer "Lung cancer") on 22 December 2014 in Crawford, Colorado, at the age of 70.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-Indep23dec14-1)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-66) He smoked two packs of cigarettes a day until he quit in 1991.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-67)

In November 2025, Cocker was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame by [Bryan Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Adams "Bryan Adams").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Cocker#cite_note-68)
